bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第207卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 207.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 207.

sentences.zh: 卷第二百七

translations.literal: Volume Two Hundred Seven.
translations.idiomatic: Volume 207.

sentences.zh: 【唐紀二十三】 起上章困敦七月，盡旃蒙大荒落正月，凡四年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 23] It begins in the seventh month of Shangzhang Kundun and runs through the first month of Zhanmeng Dahuangluo, in all a little more than four years.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 23] From the seventh month of Shangzhang Kundun through the first month of Zhanmeng Dahuangluo—about four years and a fraction.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，獻俘於含樞殿。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, captives were presented at Huanqiao Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, captives were presented at Huanqiao Hall.

sentences.zh: 太后以楷固爲左玉鈐衞大將軍、燕國公，賜姓武氏。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager made Kaigu Grand General of the Left Jade Talisman Guard and Duke of Yan, granting him the surname Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager made Kaigu Grand General of the Left Jade Talisman Guard and Duke of Yan, and granted him the surname Wu.

sentences.zh: 召公卿合宴，舉觴屬仁傑曰：「公之功也。」

translations.literal: She summoned the ministers for a joint banquet, raised her cup and turned to Di Renjie, saying, "This is your achievement."
translations.idiomatic: She summoned the chief ministers to a banquet, raised her cup, and turned to Di Renjie. "This is your achievement," she said.

sentences.zh: 將賞之，對曰：「此乃陛下威靈，將帥盡力，臣何功之有！」

translations.literal: When she was about to reward him, he replied, "This is Your Majesty's august authority and the generals' full exertion—what achievement have I!"
translations.idiomatic: As she was about to reward him, he replied, "This is Your Majesty's august authority and the generals' full exertion—what achievement is mine?"

sentences.zh: 固辭不受。

translations.literal: He firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 閏月，戊寅，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on wuyin, the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on wuyin, the imperial carriage returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以天官侍郎張錫爲鳳閣侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On jichou, Tian Guan Vice Minister Zhang Xi was made Fengge Vice Minister and Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Zhang Xi, Vice Minister of the Bureau of Celestial Offices, was appointed Fengge Vice Minister and Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State.

sentences.zh: 鸞臺侍郎、同平章事李嶠罷爲成均祭酒。

translations.literal: Luantai Vice Minister and Fellow Assessor Li Jiao was removed and made Libationer of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiao, Luantai Vice Minister and Fellow Assessor, was dismissed and made Libationer of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 錫，嶠之舅也，故罷嶠政事。

translations.literal: Xi was Jiao's maternal uncle; therefore Jiao was removed from affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was Jiao's maternal uncle, and so Jiao was removed from government.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，吐蕃將麴莽布支寇涼州，圍昌松，隴右諸軍大使唐休璟與戰於洪源谷。

translations.literal: On dingyou, the Tibetan general Qumang Buzhi raided Liang Prefecture and besieged Changsong; Tang Xiujing, Grand Military Commissioner of Longyou, fought him at Hongyuan Valley.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, the Tibetan general Qumang Buzhi raided Liang Prefecture and besieged Changsong. Tang Xiujing, Grand Military Commissioner of Longyou, engaged him at Hongyuan Valley.

sentences.zh: 麴莽布支兵甲鮮華，休璟謂諸將曰：「諸論既死，麴莽布支新爲將，不習軍事，諸貴臣子弟皆從之，望之雖如精銳，實易與耳，請爲諸君破之。」

translations.literal: Qumang Buzhi's arms and armor were fresh and splendid. Xiujing said to the generals, "Lun has already died; Qumang Buzhi is newly made commander and unskilled in military affairs. The sons of noble ministers all follow him. Though they look like elite troops, they are in fact easy to deal with. Allow me to break them for you."
translations.idiomatic: Qumang Buzhi's troops were splendidly equipped. Xiujing told his officers, "Lun is dead, and Qumang Buzhi is a new commander who does not know warfare. The sons of great ministers follow him. They may look like crack troops, but they are easy to beat. Let me break them for you."

sentences.zh: 乃被甲先陷陳，六戰皆捷，吐蕃大奔，斬首二千五百級，獲二裨將而還。

translations.literal: He then donned armor and was first to pierce the enemy line. In six battles all were victorious; the Tibetans fled in great disorder. Two thousand five hundred heads were cut off, two sub-generals were captured, and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: He donned armor and was first into the enemy ranks. Six engagements, six victories—the Tibetans broke and ran. He took twenty-five hundred heads, captured two sub-generals, and returned.

sentences.zh: 司府少卿楊元亨，尚食奉御楊元禧，皆弘武之子也。

translations.literal: Director of the Court of the Imperial Studs Yang Yuanheng and Imperial Provisioner Yang Yuanxi were both sons of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuanheng, Director of the Court of the Imperial Studs, and Yang Yuanxi, Imperial Provisioner, were both sons of Yang Hongwu.

sentences.zh: 元禧嘗忤張易之，易之言於太后：「元禧，楊素之族；

translations.literal: Yuanxi had once offended Zhang Yizhi. Yizhi said to the Empress Dowager, "Yuanxi is of the clan of Yang Su.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxi had once offended Zhang Yizhi, who told the Empress Dowager, "Yuanxi belongs to the clan of Yang Su.

sentences.zh: 素父子，隋之逆臣，子孫不應供奉。」

translations.literal: Su and his son were rebellious ministers of Sui; their descendants ought not to serve at court."
translations.idiomatic: Su and his son were traitors of the Sui; their descendants ought not hold office at the capital."

sentences.zh: 太后從之，壬寅，制：「楊素及其兄弟子孫皆不得任京官。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager assented. On renyin an edict stated, "Yang Su and his brothers' descendants may not hold capital offices."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager agreed. On renyin an edict declared that Yang Su and all his brothers' descendants were barred from capital office.

sentences.zh: 左遷元亨睦州刺史，元禧貝州刺史。

translations.literal: Yuanheng was demoted to Prefect of Muzhou, Yuanxi to Prefect of Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanheng was demoted to Prefect of Muzhou and Yuanxi to Prefect of Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以魏元忠爲隴右諸軍大使，擊吐蕃。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Wei Yuanzhong was made Grand Military Commissioner of all Longyou armies to strike the Tibetans.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Wei Yuanzhong was appointed Grand Military Commissioner of Longyou to attack the Tibetans.

sentences.zh: 庚申，太后欲造大像，使天下僧尼日出一錢以助其功。

translations.literal: On gengshen, the Empress Dowager wished to erect a great image and ordered the monks of the realm to contribute one cash per day to aid the work.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, the Empress Dowager wished to build a colossal Buddha image and ordered monks throughout the realm to give one cash a day toward the project.

sentences.zh: 狄仁傑上疏諫，其略曰：「今之伽藍，制過宮闕。

translations.literal: Di Renjie submitted a memorial remonstrating, in summary saying, "Today's monasteries in scale surpass the palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Di Renjie submitted a memorial of remonstrance, writing in part, "Monasteries today exceed the palaces in scale.

sentences.zh: 功不使鬼，止在役人，物不天來，終須地出，不損百姓，將何以求！」

translations.literal: The labor does not employ ghosts but only conscripts men; goods do not come from heaven but must finally come from the earth. If the people are not burdened, how will you obtain them!"
translations.idiomatic: No spirits do the work—only conscripted men. Nothing falls from heaven; everything must come from the land. Without taxing the people, how can it be done?"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「游僧皆托佛法，詿誤生人；

translations.literal: He also said, "Itinerant monks all rely on the Buddhist Law to deceive and mislead the living.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "Itinerant monks all cloak themselves in the Dharma to mislead the people.

sentences.zh: 裡陌動有經坊，闤闠亦立精舍。

translations.literal: In lanes and alleys scripture halls spring up at every turn; in marketplaces monasteries are also erected.
translations.idiomatic: Scripture halls appear on every lane; monasteries rise even in the marketplaces.

sentences.zh: 化誘所急，切於官征；

translations.literal: What conversion and enticement urgently require is stricter than official levies.
translations.idiomatic: What conversion demands is collected more sharply than government taxes.

sentences.zh: 法事所須，嚴於制敕。」

translations.literal: What Buddhist rites require is more stringent than imperial edicts."
translations.idiomatic: What ritual requires is enforced more strictly than imperial decrees."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「梁武、簡文捨施無限，及三淮沸浪，五嶺騰煙，列剎盈衢，無救危亡之禍，緇衣蔽路，豈有勤王之師！」

translations.literal: He also said, "Emperor Wu of Liang and Emperor Jianwen gave without limit, yet when the three Huai boiled like waves and the five Ridges sent up smoke, monasteries lined the streets and could not avert the calamity of peril and ruin; black-robed monks blocked the roads—where were armies loyal to the throne!"
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "Emperor Wu and Emperor Jianwen of Liang gave without limit, yet when the Huai ran wild and smoke rose over the Lingnan, temples lined every street and could not avert ruin. Monks in black filled the roads—where were armies loyal to the throne?"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「雖斂僧錢，百未支一。

translations.literal: He also said, "Though you collect monks' money, not one part in a hundred will suffice.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "Even if you levy money from the monks, not one part in a hundred will suffice.

sentences.zh: 尊容既廣，不可露居，覆以百層，尚憂未遍，自餘廊宇，不得全無。

translations.literal: Once the sacred image is vast, it cannot dwell in the open; though roofed with a hundred layers, one still fears it is not covered enough, and the remaining halls and corridors cannot be entirely dispensed with.
translations.idiomatic: Once the image is vast, it cannot stand in the open. A roof of a hundred layers may still not cover it, and the halls and corridors around it cannot be omitted.

sentences.zh: 如來設教，以慈悲爲主。

translations.literal: When the Tathagata established the teaching, compassion was primary.
translations.idiomatic: When the Buddha taught, compassion was his chief aim.

sentences.zh: 豈欲勞人，以存虛飾？」

translations.literal: Would he wish to weary men to preserve empty ornament?"
translations.idiomatic: Would he wish to burden people merely to preserve empty display?"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「比來水旱不節，當今邊境未寧，若費官財，又盡人力，一隅有難，將何以救之！」

translations.literal: He also said, "Recently floods and droughts have been untimely; the borders are not yet at peace. If official funds are spent and human strength exhausted, when trouble arises in one corner, how will you rescue it!"
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "Floods and droughts have come out of season, and the frontiers are still unsettled. If you spend the treasury and exhaust the people, when trouble strikes in one quarter, how will you answer it?"

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「公教朕爲善，何得相違！」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said, "You teach Us to do good—how can you go against Us!"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "You teach me to do good—how can you oppose me?"

sentences.zh: 遂罷其役。

translations.literal: She then halted the project.
translations.idiomatic: She then halted the project.

sentences.zh: 阿悉吉薄露叛，遣左金吾將軍田揚名、殿中侍御史封思業討之。

translations.literal: Ashiji Bolu rebelled; the Left Golden Crow General Tian Yangming and Palace Attendant Censor Feng Siye were sent to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When Ashiji Bolu rebelled, the court sent Tian Yangming, General of the Left Golden Crow Guard, and Feng Siye, Palace Attendant Censor, against him.

sentences.zh: 軍至碎葉，薄露夜於城傍剽掠而去，思業將騎追之，反爲所敗。

translations.literal: When the army reached Suyab, Bolu by night raided beside the city and withdrew; Siye led cavalry in pursuit and was in turn defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Suyab, Bolu raided by night near the walls and withdrew. Siye pursued with cavalry and was beaten in turn.

sentences.zh: 揚名引西突厥斛瑟羅之眾攻其城，旬餘，不克。

translations.literal: Yangming brought the forces of the Western Türk Quluo to attack his city; after more than ten days he could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Yangming brought Quluo of the Western Türks to besiege the city, but after more than ten days could not take it.

sentences.zh: 九月，薄露詐降，思業誘而斬之，遂俘其眾。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Bolu feigned surrender; Siye lured him and beheaded him, then captured his followers.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Bolu feigned surrender. Siye lured him out and beheaded him, then took his followers prisoner.

sentences.zh: 太后信重內史梁文惠公狄仁傑，群臣莫及，常謂之國老而不名。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager trusted and honored Inner Scribe Duke of Liang, Marquis of Literary Grace, Di Renjie; no minister matched him. She commonly called him State Elder and did not use his name.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager trusted and honored Di Renjie, Inner Scribe and Duke of Liang, Marquis of Literary Grace, above all other ministers. She called him State Elder and never used his name.

sentences.zh: 仁傑好面引廷爭，太后每屈意從之。

translations.literal: Renjie was fond of openly leading court debate; the Empress Dowager often yielded her intent and followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie was fond of open debate in court, and the Empress Dowager often yielded to him.

sentences.zh: 嘗從太后游幸，遇風吹仁傑巾墜，而馬驚不能止，太后命太子追執其鞚而系之。

translations.literal: Once when accompanying the Empress Dowager on an excursion, wind blew Renjie's cap off and his horse panicked and could not be stopped. The Empress Dowager ordered the Crown Prince to pursue, seize the bridle, and tie it fast.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while accompanying the Empress Dowager on an outing, wind blew Renjie's cap off and his horse bolted. She ordered the Crown Prince to ride after him, seize the bridle, and tie it fast.

sentences.zh: 仁傑屢以老疾乞骸骨，太后不許。

translations.literal: Renjie repeatedly begged to retire on account of age and illness; the Empress Dowager would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie repeatedly asked to retire on account of age and illness, but the Empress Dowager would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 入見，常止其拜，曰：「每見公拜，朕亦身痛。」

translations.literal: When he came in audience she commonly stopped his bowing, saying, "Whenever I see you bow, I too feel pain in my body."
translations.idiomatic: When he came to audience she often stopped him from bowing. "Whenever I see you bow," she said, "my own body aches."

sentences.zh: 仍免其宿直，戒其同僚曰：「自非軍國大事，勿以煩公。」

translations.literal: She also exempted him from night duty at court and warned his colleagues, "Unless it is a matter of army and state, do not trouble him."
translations.idiomatic: She also exempted him from night duty and warned his colleagues, "Unless it is a matter of army and state, do not trouble him."

sentences.zh: 辛丑，薨，太后泣曰：「朝堂空矣！」

translations.literal: On xinchou he died. The Empress Dowager wept and said, "The court hall is empty!"
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou he died. The Empress Dowager wept and said, "The court is empty!"

sentences.zh: 自是朝廷有大事，眾或不能決，太后輒歎曰：「天奪吾國老何太早邪！」

translations.literal: From then on, when the court had a great affair and the multitude could not decide, the Empress Dowager would sigh and say, "Heaven has taken Our State Elder—how too soon!"
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, whenever a great matter arose and the court could not decide, the Empress Dowager would sigh, "Heaven has taken my State Elder far too soon!"

sentences.zh: 太后嘗問仁傑：「朕欲得一佳士用之，誰可者？」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager once asked Renjie, "We wish to obtain an excellent man to employ—who will do?"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager once asked Renjie, "I wish to find an excellent man to employ. Who will do?"

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：「未審陛下欲何所用之？」

translations.literal: Renjie said, "I do not yet know what Your Majesty wishes to use him for."
translations.idiomatic: Renjie said, "I do not yet know what Your Majesty wishes to use him for."

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「欲用爲將相。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said, "We wish to use him as general or minister."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "I wish to use him as general or minister."

sentences.zh: 仁傑對曰：「文學縕藉，則蘇味道、李嶠固其選矣。

translations.literal: Renjie replied, "For literary cultivation and gentle breeding, Su Weidao and Li Jiao are certainly the choice.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie replied, "For literary polish and gentle breeding, Su Weidao and Li Jiao are certainly fit.

sentences.zh: 必欲取卓犖奇才，則有荊州長史張柬之，其人雖老，宰相才也。」

translations.literal: If you must take an outstanding extraordinary talent, there is Zhang Jianzhi, Chief of Jing Prefecture—though the man is old, he has the talent of a chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: If you want an outstanding talent, there is Zhang Jianzhi, Chief of Jing Prefecture. He is old, but he has the makings of a chief minister."

sentences.zh: 太后擢柬之爲洛州司馬。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager promoted Jianzhi to Military Administrator of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager promoted Jianzhi to Military Administrator of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 數日，又問仁傑，對曰：「前薦柬之，尚未用也。」

translations.literal: Several days later she again asked Renjie. He replied, "I previously recommended Jianzhi, yet he has not yet been employed."
translations.idiomatic: Several days later she asked Renjie again. He replied, "I recommended Jianzhi before, yet he has not been employed."

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「已遷矣。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said, "He has already been transferred."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "He has already been transferred."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣所薦者可爲宰相，非司馬也。」

translations.literal: He replied, "The man I recommended can serve as chief minister, not as military administrator."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The man I recommended can serve as chief minister, not as military administrator."

sentences.zh: 乃遷秋官侍郎；

translations.literal: Jianzhi was then transferred to Vice Minister of the Autumn Office.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhi was then made Vice Minister of the Autumn Office.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒用爲相。

translations.literal: After a long time he was finally employed as minister.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was finally made chief minister.

sentences.zh: 仁傑又嘗薦夏官侍郎姚元崇、監察御史曲阿桓彥范、太州刺史敬暉等數十人，率爲名臣。

translations.literal: Renjie also once recommended Vice Minister of the Summer Office Yao Yuanchong, Investigating Censor Huan Yanfan of Qu'a, Prefect of Tai Prefecture Jing Hui, and several dozen others; nearly all became famed ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie also recommended Yao Yuanchong, Vice Minister of the Summer Office; Huan Yanfan of Qu'a, Investigating Censor; Jing Hui, Prefect of Tai Prefecture; and dozens of others—nearly all became famed ministers.

sentences.zh: 或謂仁傑曰：「天下桃李，悉在公門矣。」

translations.literal: Someone said to Renjie, "All the peaches and plums under heaven are in your gate."
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Renjie, "All the talent under heaven is in your gate."

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：「薦賢爲國，非爲私也。」

translations.literal: Renjie said, "Recommending the worthy is for the state, not for private ends."
translations.idiomatic: Renjie said, "I recommend the worthy for the state, not for myself."

sentences.zh: 初，仁傑爲魏州刺史，有惠政，百姓爲之立生祠。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Renjie was Prefect of Wei Prefecture, he had benevolent administration and the people erected a living shrine to him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Renjie was Prefect of Wei Prefecture, his rule was benevolent and the people erected a living shrine to him.

sentences.zh: -{後}-其子景暉爲魏州司功參軍，貪暴爲人患，人遂毀其像焉。

translations.literal: Later his son Jinghui served as Siege-Official of Wei Prefecture, greedy and violent and a scourge to men; the people then destroyed the image.
translations.idiomatic: Later his son Jinghui served as Siege-Official of Wei Prefecture. Greedy and brutal, he became a scourge to the people, and they destroyed the image.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛亥，以魏元忠爲蕭關道大總管，以備突厥。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on xinhai, Wei Yuanzhong was made Grand Commander of the Xiaoguan Route to guard against the Türks.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on xinhai, Wei Yuanzhong was made Grand Commander of the Xiaoguan Route to guard against the Türks.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，制復以正月爲十一月，一月爲正月，赦天下。

translations.literal: On jiayin an edict again made the first month the eleventh month and the first month of the year the first month, and amnestied the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin an edict restored the calendar so that what had been the first month became the eleventh and the year's first month became the first again, and the realm was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，納言韋巨源罷，以文昌右丞韋安石爲鸞臺侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Censor-in-Chief Wei Juyuan was removed; Wenchang Right Assistant Wei Anshi was made Luantai Vice Minister and Fellow Assessor.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Censor-in-Chief Wei Juyuan was dismissed, and Wenchang Right Assistant Wei Anshi was made Luantai Vice Minister and Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State.

sentences.zh: 安石，津之孫也。

translations.literal: Anshi was the grandson of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi was a grandson of Wei Jin.

sentences.zh: 時武三思、張易之兄弟用事，安石數面折之。

translations.literal: At the time Wu Sansi and the Zhang Yizhi brothers held power; Anshi repeatedly confronted them to their faces.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wu Sansi and the Zhang Yizhi brothers held power, and Anshi repeatedly confronted them in open court.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍宴禁中，易之引蜀商宋霸子等數人在座同博。

translations.literal: Once when attending a banquet within the Forbidden Precinct, Yizhi brought several Sichuan merchants such as Song Bazi to sit and gamble together.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while attending a banquet in the palace, Yizhi seated several Sichuan merchants, including Song Bazi, to gamble with him.

sentences.zh: 安石跪奏曰：「商賈賤類，不應得預此會。」

translations.literal: Anshi knelt and memorialized, "Merchants are a base sort and ought not to take part in this gathering."
translations.idiomatic: Anshi knelt and said, "Merchants are a base sort and ought not to be present at this gathering."

sentences.zh: 顧左右逐出之，座中皆失色；

translations.literal: He looked to left and right to have them driven out; all at the seats changed color.
translations.idiomatic: He looked about and had them driven out. Everyone at the table turned pale.

sentences.zh: 太后以其言直，勞勉之，同列皆歎服。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager, because his words were straight, comforted and encouraged him; his colleagues all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager, pleased by his blunt honesty, comforted and praised him, and his colleagues marveled.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，太后幸新安；

translations.literal: On dingmao the Empress Dowager visited Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao the Empress Dowager visited Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 壬申，還宮。

translations.literal: On renshen she returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen she returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲寅，突厥掠隴右諸監馬萬餘匹而去。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jiayin, the Türks plundered more than ten thousand horses of the Longyou stud farms and departed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiayin, the Türks raided the Longyou stud farms and drove off more than ten thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 時屠禁尚未解，鳳閣舍人全節崔融上言，以爲：「割烹犧牲，弋獵禽獸，聖人著之典禮，不可廢闕。

translations.literal: At the time the ban on slaughter had not yet been lifted. Fengge Attendant Quanjie Cui Rong submitted a statement, holding that "cutting and cooking sacrificial victims and shooting and hunting birds and beasts—the sages set these forth in canonical ritual and they cannot be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The ban on slaughter had not yet been lifted. Cui Rong, Fengge Attendant of Quanjie, submitted a memorial arguing that cutting sacrificial victims and hunting birds and beasts were set forth by the sages in canonical ritual and could not be abolished.

sentences.zh: 又，江南食魚，河西食肉，一日不可無；

translations.literal: Moreover, south of the Yangzi they eat fish; west of the He they eat meat—one day cannot be without them.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, south of the Yangzi people live on fish, and west of the He they live on meat; neither can do without them for a day.

sentences.zh: 富者未革，貧者難堪，況貧賤之人，仰屠爲生，日戮一人，終不能絶，但資恐喝，徒長奸欺。

translations.literal: The rich have not changed their ways; the poor can hardly bear it. Moreover, poor and base men rely on slaughter for a living—slaughtering one person a day, it can never be ended; it only supplies intimidation and vainly fosters deceit.
translations.idiomatic: The rich have not changed, while the poor can hardly endure it. Poor men who live by the butcher's trade cannot be stopped from killing day after day; the ban only breeds intimidation and fraud.

sentences.zh: 爲政者苟順月令，合禮經，自然物遂其生，人得其性矣。」

translations.literal: If those who govern would only follow the monthly ordinances and accord with the ritual classics, naturally things would fulfill their lives and men would obtain their natures."
translations.idiomatic: If rulers would follow the seasonal ordinances and conform to the ritual classics, things would fulfill their nature and men would live as they ought.

sentences.zh: 戊午，復開屠禁，祠祭用牲牢如故。

translations.literal: On wuwu the ban on slaughter was reopened; sacrifices again used victims and livestock as before.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu the slaughter ban was lifted, and sacrifices again used victims and livestock as before.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁丑，以成州言佛跡見，改元大足。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on dingchou, because Cheng Prefecture reported that a Buddha's footprint had appeared, the era name was changed to Dazu.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on dingchou, because Cheng Prefecture reported that a Buddha's footprint had appeared, the era name was changed to Dazu.

sentences.zh: 二月，己酉，以鸞臺侍郎柏人李懷遠同平章事。

translations.literal: In the second month, on jiyou, Luantai Vice Minister Li Huaiyuan of Bairen was made Fellow Assessor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jiyou, Li Huaiyuan of Bairen, Luantai Vice Minister, was made Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State.

sentences.zh: 三月，鳳閣侍郎、同平章事張錫坐知選漏洩禁中語、贓滿數萬，當斬，臨刑釋之，流循州。

translations.literal: In the third month, Fengge Vice Minister and Fellow Assessor Zhang Xi, on account of knowing selection matters and leaking forbidden-palace speech, with bribes amounting to tens of thousands, deserved decapitation; at the moment of execution he was released and banished to Xun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Zhang Xi, Fengge Vice Minister and Fellow Assessor, was found guilty of leaking palace secrets related to official selection and of taking bribes of tens of thousands. He was sentenced to decapitation, but at the scaffold he was spared and banished to Xun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時蘇味道亦坐事與錫俱下司刑獄，錫乘馬，氣色自若，捨於三品院，帷屏食飲，無異平居。

translations.literal: At the time Su Weidao was also implicated and entered the Ministry of Justice prison with Xi. Xi rode a horse, his complexion as if at ease; he was lodged in the Third-Rank Courtyard with curtains and screens, food and drink no different from ordinary days.
translations.idiomatic: Su Weidao was implicated at the same time and entered the Ministry of Justice prison with Xi. Xi rode to prison looking perfectly at ease. He was lodged in the Third-Rank Courtyard with curtains and screens, and ate and drank as in ordinary life.

sentences.zh: 味道步至系所，席地而臥，蔬食而已。

translations.literal: Weidao walked to the place of detention, slept on the ground, and ate only vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: Weidao walked to the jail, slept on the ground, and ate only plain vegetables.

sentences.zh: 太后聞之，赦味道，復其位。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager heard of it, she pardoned Weidao and restored his post.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager heard of it, she pardoned Weidao and restored him to office.

sentences.zh: 是月，大雪，蘇味道以爲瑞，帥百官入賀。

translations.literal: That month there was heavy snow. Su Weidao took it as an auspice and led the hundred officials in to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: That month brought heavy snow. Su Weidao took it as a good omen and led the officials in to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史王求禮止之曰：「三月雪爲瑞雪，臘月雷爲瑞雷乎？」

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Censor Wang Qiuli stopped him, saying, "If snow in the third month is auspicious snow, is thunder in the twelfth month auspicious thunder?"
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Censor Wang Qiuli stopped him. "If snow in the third month is an auspicious snow," he said, "is thunder in the twelfth month an auspicious thunder?"

sentences.zh: 味道不從。

translations.literal: Weidao did not follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Weidao would not listen.

sentences.zh: 既入，求禮獨不賀，進言曰：「今陽和布氣，草木發榮，而寒雪爲災，豈得誣以爲瑞！

translations.literal: After they entered, Qiuli alone did not congratulate and advanced a statement, saying, "Now the yang harmony spreads its breath and grass and trees put forth glory, yet cold snow is a calamity—how can it be falsely called an auspice!
translations.idiomatic: Once inside, Qiuli alone did not congratulate. He said, "The warm breath of spring is spreading and plants are budding, yet this cold snow is a disaster. How can you call it an omen of good fortune?

sentences.zh: 賀者皆諂諛之士也。」

translations.literal: Those who congratulate are all flatterers."
translations.idiomatic: Those who congratulate are nothing but sycophants."

sentences.zh: 太后爲之罷朝。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager for this reason dismissed court.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager dismissed court on account of this.

sentences.zh: 時又有獻三足牛者，宰相復賀。

translations.literal: At the time there was also presented a three-footed ox; the chief ministers again congratulated.
translations.idiomatic: At the time someone also presented a three-legged ox, and the chief ministers congratulated again.

sentences.zh: 求禮揚言曰：「凡物反常皆爲妖。

translations.literal: Qiuli proclaimed aloud, "Whenever a thing is contrary to the norm it is a portent.
translations.idiomatic: Qiuli declared aloud, "Whenever a thing is contrary to nature it is an omen of ill.

sentences.zh: 此鼎足非其人，政教不行之象也。」

translations.literal: These tripod legs are not the right men—it is the image of government and teaching not being carried out."
translations.idiomatic: These tripod legs are not the right men—it is a sign that government and teaching are not being carried out."

sentences.zh: 太后爲之愀然。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager on account of this looked grave.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager looked grave at this.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，乙亥，太后幸三陽宮。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on yihai, the Empress Dowager visited Sanyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fifth month, on yihai, the Empress Dowager visited Sanyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 以魏元忠爲靈武道行軍大總管，以備突厥。

translations.literal: Wei Yuanzhong was made Grand Commander of the Lingwu Route marching armies to guard against the Türks.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuanzhong was appointed Grand Commander of the Lingwu Route armies to guard against the Türks.

sentences.zh: 天官侍郎鹽官顧琮同平章事。

translations.literal: Tian Guan Vice Minister Gu Cong of Yanguan was made Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Cong of Yanguan, Vice Minister of the Bureau of Celestial Offices, was made Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State.

sentences.zh: 六月，庚申，以夏官尚書李迥秀同平章事。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on gengshen, Xia Guan Minister Li Jiaoxiu was made Fellow Assessor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on gengshen, Li Jiaoxiu, Minister of the Bureau of Summer Offices, was made Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State.

sentences.zh: 迥秀性至孝，其母本微賤，妻崔氏常叱媵婢，母聞之不悅，迥秀即時出之。

translations.literal: Jiaoxiu was by nature extremely filial. His mother had originally been of humble and low status; his wife, the Lady Cui, often scolded the secondary wives and maidservants, and when his mother heard of it she was displeased; Jiaoxiu immediately divorced her.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaoxiu was deeply filial. His mother had come from humble origins, and his wife Lady Cui often berated the concubines and maids. When his mother heard of it she was displeased, and Jiaoxiu immediately sent his wife away.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「賢室雖不避嫌疑，然過非七出，何遽如是！」

translations.literal: Someone said, "Your worthy wife, though she did not avoid suspicion, yet her fault was not among the seven grounds for divorce—why so hastily thus!"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "Your worthy wife may not have avoided suspicion, but her fault was not among the seven grounds for divorce. Why act so hastily?"

sentences.zh: 迥秀曰：「娶妻本以養親，今乃違忤顏色，安敢留也！」

translations.literal: Jiaoxiu said, "One takes a wife originally to serve one's parents; now she has gone against their wishes—how dare I keep her!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiaoxiu replied, "One takes a wife to serve one's parents. She has now displeased my mother—how could I keep her?"

sentences.zh: 竟出之。

translations.literal: In the end he sent her away.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he divorced her.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲戌，太后還宮。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on jiaxu, the Empress Dowager returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on jiaxu, the Empress Dowager returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 甲申，李懷遠罷爲秋官尚書。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Li Huaiyuan was removed and made Autumn Official Minister.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Li Huaiyuan was dismissed and made Minister of the Bureau of Autumn Offices.

sentences.zh: 八月，突厥默啜寇邊，命安北大都護相王爲天兵道元帥，統諸軍擊之，未行而虜退。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the Türk Mochuo raided the frontier; the Great Protector of the Pacified North, the Prince of the Vicarious State, was ordered to be Grand Marshal of the Heavenly Army Route and to command all armies to strike him, but before setting out the barbarians withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, the Türk khagan Mochuo raided the frontier. The Great Protector of the Pacified North, the Prince of the Vicarious State, was ordered to serve as Grand Marshal of the Heavenly Army Route and command all armies against him, but before he set out the invaders withdrew.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，武邑人蘇安恆上疏曰：「陛下欽先聖之顧托，受嗣子之推讓，敬天順人，二十年矣。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Su Anheng of Wuyi submitted a memorial saying, "Your Majesty has revered the former sage's dying charge, accepted the heir's yielding, and honored Heaven and followed the people—for twenty years now.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Su Anheng of Wuyi submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty has honored the former sage's dying charge, accepted the heir's yielding of the throne, and followed Heaven and the people—for twenty years now.

sentences.zh: 豈不聞帝舜褰裳，周公復辟！

translations.literal: Have you not heard how Emperor Shun gathered his robe and yielded, and the Duke of Zhou restored the throne!
translations.idiomatic: Have you not heard how Emperor Shun gathered his robes to yield the throne, and the Duke of Zhou restored King Cheng to power!

sentences.zh: 舜之於禹，事只族親；

translations.literal: Shun toward Yu served only as kin within the clan;
translations.idiomatic: Shun's relationship to Yu was only that of clan kin;

sentences.zh: 旦與成王，不離叔父。

translations.literal: Dan and King Cheng never parted from the relationship of uncle and nephew.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou and King Cheng never lost the bond of uncle and nephew.

sentences.zh: 族親何如子之愛，叔父何如母之恩？

translations.literal: How can clan kin compare to a son's love, or an uncle to a mother's grace?
translations.idiomatic: How can clan kin compare with a son's love, or an uncle with a mother's devotion?

sentences.zh: 今太子孝敬是崇，春秋既壯，若使統臨宸極，何異陛下之身！

translations.literal: Now the Crown Prince honors filial piety above all, his years are already mature; if he were made to rule the imperial seat, how would it differ from Your Majesty's own person!
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince now honors filial piety above all, and he has come of age. If he were to rule the throne, would that not be the same as Your Majesty yourself?

sentences.zh: 陛下年德既尊，寶位將倦，機務繁重，浩蕩心神，何不禪位東宮，自怡聖體！

translations.literal: Your Majesty's years and virtue are already honored, the precious seat grows wearisome, state business is heavy and burdens the spirit—why not abdicate to the Eastern Palace and give ease to your sacred person!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's years and virtue are already exalted, the throne grows wearisome, and state affairs weigh heavily on your spirit. Why not abdicate to the Crown Prince and give yourself ease?

sentences.zh: 自昔理天下者，不見二姓而俱王也，當今梁、定、河內、建昌諸王，承陛下之廕覆，並得封王。

translations.literal: From antiquity those who governed All-under-Heaven have never seen two surnames both hold kingship; now the kings of Liang, Ding, Henei, Jianchang, and others, relying on Your Majesty's sheltering shade, have all received princely investiture.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity, no ruler of All-under-Heaven has seen two imperial surnames reign as kings at once. Now the Princes of Liang, Ding, Henei, Jianchang, and others, sheltered by Your Majesty, have all been enfeoffed as kings.

sentences.zh: 臣謂千秋萬歳之-{後}-，於事非便。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that in the thousand autumns and myriad years after, this will be inconvenient for affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that in ages to come this will prove inconvenient.

sentences.zh: 臣請黜爲公侯，任以閒簡。

translations.literal: Your servant asks that they be demoted to dukes and marquises and assigned to leisurely and simple posts.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that they be reduced to dukes and marquises and given unburdensome appointments.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞陛下有二十餘孫，今無尺寸之封，此非長久之計也。

translations.literal: Your servant has further heard that Your Majesty has more than twenty grandsons, yet now none has the slightest fief—this is not a plan for the long term.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that Your Majesty has more than twenty grandsons, yet none has received even the smallest fief. This is no plan for the long term.

sentences.zh: 臣請分土而王之，擇立師傅，教其孝敬之道，以夾輔周室，屏籓皇家，斯爲美矣。」

translations.literal: Your servant asks that lands be divided and they be enfeoffed as kings, that tutors be chosen and established to teach them the way of filial piety and respect, to flank and assist the Zhou house and shield the royal house—this would be beautiful indeed."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that lands be divided and your grandsons be enfeoffed as kings, with tutors chosen to teach them filial piety and respect, so they may support the imperial house as shield and screen. That would be admirable indeed."

sentences.zh: 疏奏，太后召見，賜食，慰諭而遣之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Empress Dowager summoned him for audience, gave him food, comforted and instructed him, and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the Empress Dowager summoned him, gave him a meal, comforted and praised him, and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 太后春秋高，政事多委張易之兄弟；

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager's years were advanced; she largely entrusted state affairs to the Zhang Yizhi brothers;
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager was advanced in years and largely entrusted state affairs to the Zhang Yizhi brothers;

sentences.zh: 邵王重潤與其妹永泰郡主、主婿魏王武延基竊議其事。

translations.literal: Prince Shao Chongrun, together with his sister Princess Yongtai and the princess's husband, Prince Wei Wu Yanji, privately discussed the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shao Chongrun, his sister Princess Yongtai, and the princess's husband, Prince Wei Wu Yanji, privately discussed the matter.

sentences.zh: 易之訴於太后，九月，壬申，太后皆逼令自殺。

translations.literal: Yizhi complained to the Empress Dowager; in the ninth month, on renshen, the Empress Dowager forced them all to kill themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi reported this to the Empress Dowager. In the ninth month, on renshen, she forced them all to commit suicide.

sentences.zh: 延基，承嗣之子也。

translations.literal: Yanji was the son of Chengsi.
translations.idiomatic: Yanji was a son of Wu Chengsi.

sentences.zh: 丙申，以相王知左、右羽林衞大將軍事。

translations.literal: On bingshen, the Prince of the Vicarious State was made to oversee the affairs of the Left and Right Commandants of the Feathered Forest Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, the Prince of the Vicarious State was put in charge of the Left and Right Commandants of the Feathered Forest Guard.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，壬寅，太后西入關，辛酉，至京師；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on renyin, the Empress Dowager entered the passes from the west; on xinyou she reached the capital;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on renyin, the Empress Dowager entered the passes from the west. On xinyou she reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: She amnestied the realm and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: She pardoned the realm and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 十一月，戊寅，改含元宮爲大明宮。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on wuyin, Hanyuan Palace was renamed Daming Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on wuyin, Hanyuan Palace was renamed Daming Palace.

sentences.zh: 天官侍郎安平崔玄暐，性介直，未嘗請謁。

translations.literal: Tian Guan Vice Minister Cui Xuanwei of Anping was by nature upright and unbending and had never sought audiences by petition.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuanwei of Anping, Vice Minister of the Bureau of Celestial Offices, was upright and unyielding and had never curried favor through petitions.

sentences.zh: 執政惡之，改文昌左丞。

translations.literal: The chief ministers disliked him and transferred him to Wenchang Left Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers disliked him and transferred him to Wenchang Left Assistant.

sentences.zh: 月餘，太后謂玄□曰：「自卿改官以來，聞令史設齋自慶。

translations.literal: After more than a month the Empress Dowager said to Cui Xuanwei, "Since you were changed in office, I have heard that the clerks held a feast to congratulate themselves.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month, the Empress Dowager said to Cui Xuanwei, "Since your transfer, I hear the clerks have been holding feasts to celebrate among themselves.

sentences.zh: 此欲盛爲奸貪耳，今還卿舊任。」

translations.literal: This means they want all the more to be corrupt and greedy; now we restore you to your former post."
translations.idiomatic: That means they mean to grow all the more corrupt and greedy. We now restore you to your former post."

sentences.zh: 乃復拜天官侍郎，仍賜彩七十段。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was again appointed Tian Guan Vice Minister and was further granted seventy rolls of colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Vice Minister of the Bureau of Celestial Offices and granted seventy rolls of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 以主客郎中郭元振爲涼州都督、隴右諸軍大使。

translations.literal: Master of Guests Director Guo Yuanzhen was made Military Commissioner of Liang Prefecture and Grand Commissioner of all Longyou armies.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yuanzhen, Director in the Bureau of Hosts, was appointed Military Commissioner of Liang Prefecture and Grand Commissioner of the Longyou armies.

sentences.zh: 先是，涼州南北境不過四百餘里，突厥、吐蕃頻歳奄至城下，百姓苦之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liang Prefecture's north-south extent was no more than four hundred-odd li; the Türks and Tibetans year after year suddenly arrived beneath the city walls, and the people suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Liang Prefecture's north-south extent was barely four hundred li, and the Türks and Tibetans raided to the city walls year after year. The people suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 元振始於南境硤口置和戎城，北境磧中置白亭軍，控其衝要，拓州境千五百里，自是寇不復至城下。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen first established Herong Fort at Qikou on the southern frontier and Baiting Army in the desert of the northern frontier, controlling the strategic points and extending the prefecture's territory fifteen hundred li; from then on raiders no longer reached beneath the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen first built Herong Fort at Qikou on the southern frontier and Baiting Army in the northern desert, seizing the strategic points and extending the prefecture's territory to fifteen hundred li. After that raiders no longer reached the city walls.

sentences.zh: 元振又令甘州刺史李漢通開置屯田，盡水陸之利。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen also had Li Hantong, Prefect of Gan Prefecture, open and establish military colonies, exploiting to the full the advantages of water and land.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen also had Li Hantong, Prefect of Gan Prefecture, establish military colonies and exploit the region's full agricultural potential.

sentences.zh: 舊涼州粟麥斛至數千，及漢通收率之-{後}-，一縑糴數十斛，積軍糧支數十年。

translations.literal: Formerly in Liang Prefecture a bushel of millet or wheat reached several thousand, but after Hantong collected the harvests, one bolt of silk bought several tens of bushels, and military grain accumulated enough to last several decades.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly a bushel of grain in Liang Prefecture cost thousands in cash, but after Hantong's harvests one bolt of silk bought dozens of bushels, and military stores accumulated enough to last decades.

sentences.zh: 元振善於撫御，在涼州五年，夷、夏畏慕，令行禁止，牛羊被野，路不拾遺。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen was skilled at comforting and governing; during five years in Liang Prefecture, barbarians and Chinese alike feared and admired him, orders were enforced and prohibitions observed, cattle and sheep covered the wilds, and no one picked up lost objects on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen excelled at governing and winning loyalty. During five years in Liang Prefecture, both tribesmen and Chinese feared and admired him, his orders were obeyed, cattle and sheep filled the countryside, and no one picked up lost objects on the roads.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙酉，初設武舉。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on yiyou, the military examination was first established.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on yiyou, the military examination was established for the first time.

sentences.zh: 空厥寇鹽、夏二州。

translations.literal: The Türks raided Yan and Xia Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The Türks raided Yan and Xia Prefectures.

sentences.zh: 三月，庚寅，突厥破石嶺，寇并州。

translations.literal: In the third month, on gengyin, the Türks broke through Shiling and raided Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on gengyin, the Türks broke through Shiling and raided Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以雍州長史薛季昶攝右台大夫，充山東防禦軍大使，滄、瀛、幽、易、恆、定等州諸軍皆受季昶節度。

translations.literal: Yong Prefecture Chief Administrator Xue Jichang was made Acting Censor-in-Chief of the Right Platform and Grand Commissioner of the Shandong Defense Army; all armies of Cang, Ying, You, Yi, Heng, Ding, and other prefectures were placed under Jichang's command.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Jichang, Chief Administrator of Yong Prefecture, was made Acting Censor-in-Chief of the Right Platform and Grand Commissioner of the Shandong Defense Army, and all armies in Cang, Ying, You, Yi, Heng, Ding, and other prefectures were placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，以幽州刺史張仁願專知幽、平、媯、檀防禦，仍與季昶相知，以拒突厥。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, You Prefecture Prefect Zhang Renyuan was made solely responsible for the defenses of You, Ping, Gui, and Tan, and continued to coordinate with Jichang to resist the Türks.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Zhang Renyuan, Prefect of You Prefecture, was put solely in charge of defenses in You, Ping, Gui, and Tan, and continued to coordinate with Jichang against the Türks.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬申，蘇安恆復上疏曰：「臣聞天下者，神堯、文武之天下也。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on renshen, Su Anheng again submitted a memorial saying, "Your servant has heard that All-under-Heaven is the All-under-Heaven of Divine Yao and King Wen and King Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on renshen, Su Anheng again submitted a memorial: "I have heard that All-under-Heaven belongs to Divine Yao and Kings Wen and Wu.

sentences.zh: 陛下雖居正統，實因唐氏舊基。

translations.literal: Your Majesty though occupying the orthodox succession in fact relies on the Tang house's old foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty holds the orthodox throne, but in fact you built upon the Tang foundation.

sentences.zh: 當今太子追回，年德俱盛，陛下貪其寶位而忘母子深恩，將何聖顏以見唐家宗廟，將何誥命以謁大帝墳陵？

translations.literal: Now the Crown Prince has been recalled; his years and virtue are both flourishing. Your Majesty, clinging to the precious seat and forgetting the deep grace between mother and son—with what countenance will you face the Tang clan temple, with what edict will you visit the Great Emperor's tomb and mausoleum?
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince has now been recalled, and his years and virtue are both in their prime. Yet Your Majesty clings to the throne and forgets the deep bond of mother and son. With what face will you appear before the Tang ancestral temple, and with what edict will you visit the tomb of the Great Emperor?

sentences.zh: 陛下何故日夜積憂，不知鐘鳴漏盡！

translations.literal: Why does Your Majesty day and night accumulate worry and not know that the bell has sounded and the clepsydra is empty!
translations.idiomatic: Why do you day and night accumulate worry and not see that your hour is running out?

sentences.zh: 臣愚以爲天意人事，還歸李家。

translations.literal: Your servant in his foolishness considers that Heaven's intent and human affairs all return to the Li house.
translations.idiomatic: In my foolish view, both Heaven's will and human affairs point back to the house of Li.

sentences.zh: 陛下雖安天位，殊不知物極則反，器滿則傾。

translations.literal: Your Majesty though secure in Heaven's seat still does not know that when things reach their extreme they reverse, and when a vessel is full it tips.
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Majesty sits secure on the throne, you do not see that what reaches its extreme must reverse, and a brimming vessel must spill.

sentences.zh: 臣何惜一朝之命，而不安萬乘之國哉！」

translations.literal: Why should your servant begrudge one morning's life and not secure the state of ten thousand chariots!"
translations.idiomatic: Why should I begrudge my life for a single morning and not seek to secure the realm!"

sentences.zh: 太后亦不之罪。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager did not punish him for it.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 乙未，以相王爲并州牧，充安北道行軍元帥，以魏元忠爲之副。

translations.literal: On yiwei, the Prince of the Vicarious State was made Prefect of Bing Prefecture and Grand Marshal of the Pacified North Route marching armies, with Wei Yuanzhong as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, the Prince of the Vicarious State was made Prefect of Bing and Grand Marshal of the Pacified North Route armies, with Wei Yuanzhong as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 六月，壬戌，召神都留守韋巨源詣京師，以副留守李嶠代之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on renxu, the Shendu garrison commander Wei Juyuan was summoned to the capital; Vice Garrison Commander Li Jiao replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renxu, Wei Juyuan, Garrison Commander of Shendu, was summoned to the capital, and Vice Garrison Commander Li Jiao replaced him.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲午，突厥寇代州。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on jiawu, the Türks raided Dai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on jiawu, the Türks raided Dai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 司僕卿張昌宗兄弟貴盛，勢傾朝野。

translations.literal: Chamberlain for the Imperial Stud Zhang Changzong and his brothers were honored and powerful, their influence overwhelming court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Changzong, Chamberlain for the Imperial Stud, and his brothers grew powerful and their influence overshadowed the court and the realm.

sentences.zh: 八月，戊午，太子、相王、太平公主上表請封昌宗爲王，制不許；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on wuwu, the Crown Prince, the Prince of the Vicarious State, and Princess Taiping submitted memorials asking that Changzong be enfeoffed as king; an edict did not permit it;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on wuwu, the Crown Prince, the Prince of the Vicarious State, and Princess Taiping submitted memorials asking that Changzong be made a king. An edict refused.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，又請，乃賜爵鄴國公。

translations.literal: On renxu they asked again, and he was then granted the title Duke of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu they asked again, and he was granted the title Duke of Ye.

sentences.zh: 敕：「自今有告言揚州及豫、博餘黨，一無所問，內外官司無得爲理。」

translations.literal: An edict stated, "From now on, anyone who reports persons as remnants of the Yangzhou, Yu, and Bo factions shall receive no inquiry whatsoever; inner and outer offices must not take up such cases."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared, "From now on, reports alleging remnants of the Yangzhou, Yu, and Bo factions shall not be investigated at all. No office inside or outside the court may take up such cases."

sentences.zh: 九月，乙丑朔，日有食之，不盡如鉤，神都見其既。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the first day yichou, there was an eclipse of the sun, incomplete like a hook; at Shendu its totality was seen.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the ninth month, yichou, there was a solar eclipse, the sun not fully covered and shaped like a hook. At Shendu the totality was visible.

sentences.zh: 壬申，突厥寇忻州。

translations.literal: On renshen, the Türks raided Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, the Türks raided Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 己卯，吐蕃遣其臣論彌薩來求和。

translations.literal: On jimao, the Tibetans sent their minister Lun Misai to seek peace.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, Tibet sent its minister Lun Misai to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以太子賓客武三思爲大谷道大總管，洛州長史敬暉爲副；

translations.literal: On gengchen, Crown Prince Guest-Attendant Wu Sansi was made Grand Commander of the Dayu Route, with Luozhou Chief Administrator Jing Hui as deputy;
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, Wu Sansi, Guest-Attendant of the Crown Prince, was made Grand Commander of the Dayu Route, with Jing Hui, Chief Administrator of Luozhou, as his deputy;

sentences.zh: 辛巳，又以相王旦爲并州道元帥，三思與武攸宜、魏元忠爲之副；

translations.literal: On xinsi the Prince of the Vicarious State Dan was again made Marshal of the Bing Route; Sansi, Wu Youyi, and Wei Yuanzhong served as his deputies;
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi the Prince of the Vicarious State Li Dan was again made Marshal of the Bing Route, with Sansi, Wu Youyi, and Wei Yuanzhong as his deputies;

sentences.zh: 姚元崇爲長史，司禮少卿鄭杲爲司馬；

translations.literal: Yao Yuanchong was Chief Administrator, and Sili Vice Director Zheng Gao was Army Marshal;
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yuanchong served as Chief Administrator, and Zheng Gao, Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, as Army Marshal;

sentences.zh: 然竟不行。

translations.literal: Yet in the end they did not set out.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, however, the campaign was never launched.

sentences.zh: 癸未，宴論彌薩於麟德殿。

translations.literal: On guiwei Lun Misai was feasted at Linde Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei the court held a banquet for Lun Misai at Linde Hall.

sentences.zh: 時涼州都督唐休璟入朝，亦預宴。

translations.literal: At the time Liang Prefecture Military Commissioner Tang Xiujing had come to court and also attended the banquet.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Tang Xiujing, Military Commissioner of Liang Prefecture, was at court and also attended the banquet.

sentences.zh: 彌薩屢窺之。

translations.literal: Misai repeatedly looked at him stealthily.
translations.idiomatic: Misai kept stealing glances at him.

sentences.zh: 太后問其故，對曰：「洪源之戰，此將軍猛厲無故，故欲識之。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager asked the reason; he replied, "At the battle of Hongyuan this general was fiercely unstoppable—I wished therefore to recognize him."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager asked why. He replied, "At the battle of Hongyuan this general fought with relentless fury. I wanted to see who he was."

sentences.zh: 太后擢休璟爲右武威、金吾二衞大將軍。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager promoted Xiujing to Grand General of the Right Martial Prestige and Golden Grips guards.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager promoted Xiujing to Grand General of both the Right Martial Prestige Guard and the Golden Grips Guard.

sentences.zh: 休璟練習邊事，自碣石以西逾四鎮，綿亙萬里，山川要害，皆能記之。

translations.literal: Xiujing was versed in frontier affairs; from Jieshi westward beyond the Four Garrisons, stretching ten thousand li, he could remember every strategic point of mountain and river.
translations.idiomatic: Xiujing was thoroughly versed in frontier affairs. From Jieshi westward beyond the Four Garrisons, across ten thousand li of terrain, he knew every strategic mountain pass and river crossing by heart.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲辰，天官侍郎、同平章事顧琮薨。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiachen, Tian Guan Vice Minister and Fellow Assessor Gu Cong died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on jiachen, Gu Cong, Vice Minister of the Bureau of Celestial Offices and Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State, died.

sentences.zh: 戊申，吐蕃贊普將萬餘人寇茂州，都督陳大慈與之四戰，皆破之，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: On wushen the Tibetan king led more than ten thousand men to raid Mao Prefecture; Military Commissioner Chen Daci fought him four times and each time defeated him, beheading more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen the Tibetan king led more than ten thousand men to raid Mao Prefecture. Military Commissioner Chen Daci fought four battles and defeated him each time, taking more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛未，監察御史魏靖上疏，以爲：「陛下既知來俊臣之奸，處以極法，乞詳覆俊臣等所推十獄，伸其枉濫。」

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on xinwei, Investigating Censor Wei Jing submitted a memorial, arguing, "Your Majesty, having known Lai Junchen's treachery and punished him with the extreme law, I beg that the ten cases pushed by Junchen and others be thoroughly reviewed and their wrongful excesses redressed."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on xinwei, Investigating Censor Wei Jing submitted a memorial arguing, "Your Majesty, now that you have recognized Lai Junchen's treachery and executed him, I ask that the ten cases he and his followers prosecuted be thoroughly reviewed and wrongful convictions cleared."

sentences.zh: 太后乃命監察御史蘇頲按覆俊臣等舊獄，由是雪免者甚眾。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager thereupon ordered Investigating Censor Su Ting to review the old cases of Junchen and others, and thereby those cleared and pardoned were very many.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager then ordered Investigating Censor Su Ting to review Junchen's old cases, and very many were cleared and pardoned as a result.

sentences.zh: 頲，夔之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Ting was the great-grandson of Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Su Ting was a great-grandson of Su Kui.

sentences.zh: 戊子，太后祀南郊，赦天下。

translations.literal: On wuzi the Empress Dowager sacrificed at the Southern Suburban Altar and amnestied the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi the Empress Dowager performed the southern suburban sacrifice and pardoned the realm.

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲午，以魏元忠爲安東道安撫大使，羽林衞大將軍李多祚檢校幽州都督，右羽林衞將軍薛訥、左武衞將軍駱務整爲之副。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jiawu, Wei Yuanzhong was made Pacification Commissioner of the Andong Route; Grand General of the Feathered Forest Guard Li Duozuo was made acting Military Commissioner of You Prefecture, with Right Feathered Forest Guard General Xue Ne and Left Martial Guard General Luo Wuzheng as deputies.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiawu, Wei Yuanzhong was made Pacification Commissioner of the Andong Route. Li Duozuo, Grand General of the Feathered Forest Guard, was made acting Military Commissioner of You Prefecture, with Xue Ne, General of the Right Feathered Forest Guard, and Luo Wuzheng, General of the Left Martial Guard, as deputies.

sentences.zh: 戊申，置北庭都護府於庭州。

translations.literal: On wushen the North Court Protectorate was established at Ting Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen the North Court Protectorate was established at Ting Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 侍御史張循憲爲河東採訪使，有疑事不能決，病之，問侍吏曰：「此有佳客，可與議事者乎？」

translations.literal: Attending Censor Zhang Xunxian was a Hedong Circuit Investigating Commissioner; when he had doubtful matters he could not decide he was distressed and asked his attendant clerk, "Is there an excellent guest here with whom one can discuss affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor Zhang Xunxian served as Hedong Circuit Investigating Commissioner. Troubled by a case he could not resolve, he asked his attendant clerk, "Is there a capable visitor here I can discuss this with?"

sentences.zh: 吏言前平鄕尉猗氏張嘉貞有異才，循憲召見，詢以事；

translations.literal: The clerk said that former Pingxiang Captain Zhang Jiazhen of Yishi had extraordinary talent; Xunxian summoned and met him and inquired about the matter;
translations.idiomatic: The clerk said that Zhang Jiazhen of Yishi, former Captain of Pingxiang, had extraordinary talent. Xunxian summoned him and questioned him about the case;

sentences.zh: 嘉貞爲條析理分，莫不洗然。

translations.literal: Jiazhen analyzed each point and sorted the reasoning, and nothing was not made clear.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen analyzed each point with lucid reasoning, and everything became clear.

sentences.zh: 循憲因請爲奏，皆意所未及。

translations.literal: Xunxian then asked him to draft memorials; all reached points Xunxian had not thought of.
translations.idiomatic: Xunxian then had him draft memorials, and Jiazhen's points went beyond anything Xunxian had considered.

sentences.zh: 循憲還，見太后，太后善其奏，循憲具言嘉貞所爲，且請以己之官授之。

translations.literal: When Xunxian returned and saw the Empress Dowager, she praised his memorials; Xunxian fully explained what Jiazhen had done and asked moreover to confer his own office upon him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xunxian returned and met the Empress Dowager, she praised his memorials. Xunxian explained fully what Jiazhen had done and asked to give Jiazhen his own office.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「朕寧無一官自進賢邪！」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said, "Would We have no office with which to advance the worthy ourselves!"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "Do you think I have no office with which to advance the worthy myself?"

sentences.zh: 因召嘉貞，入見內殿，與語，大悅，即拜監察御史；

translations.literal: Thereupon Jiazhen was summoned; he entered and was received in the inner hall, and when she spoke with him she was greatly pleased and immediately appointed him Investigating Censor;
translations.idiomatic: She summoned Jiazhen to the inner hall. Delighted after speaking with him, she immediately appointed him Investigating Censor;

sentences.zh: 擢循憲司勳郎中，賞其得人也。

translations.literal: Xunxian was promoted to Director in the Bureau of Meritorious Service, rewarding him for finding the man.
translations.idiomatic: Xunxian was promoted to Director in the Bureau of Meritorious Service, rewarded for having found the right man.

sentences.zh: 春，三月，壬戌朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In spring, the third month, on the first day renxu, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the third month, on the first day renxu, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，吐蕃遣使獻馬千匹、金二千兩以求昏。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, the Tibetans sent envoys presenting a thousand horses and two thousand taels of gold to seek marriage.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Tibet sent envoys offering a thousand horses and two thousand taels of gold to request a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 閏月，丁丑，命韋安石留守神都。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on dingchou, Wei Anshi was ordered to remain on garrison duty at Shendu.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on dingchou, Wei Anshi was ordered to remain as garrison commander at Shendu.

sentences.zh: 己卯，改文昌台爲中台。

translations.literal: On jimao the Wenchang Platform was renamed the Central Platform.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao the Wenchang Platform was renamed the Central Platform.

sentences.zh: 以中台左丞李嶠知納言事。

translations.literal: Zhongtai Left Assistant Li Jiao was made to oversee the affairs of the Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiao, Left Assistant of the Central Platform, was put in charge of the affairs of the Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 新羅王金理洪卒，遣使立其弟崇基爲王。

translations.literal: King Jin Lihong of Silla died; envoys were sent to install his younger brother Chongji as king.
translations.idiomatic: King Jin Lihong of Silla died, and envoys were sent to install his younger brother Chongji as king.

sentences.zh: 六月，辛酉，突厥默啜遣其臣莫賀干來，請以女妻皇太子之子。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on xinyou, the Türk Mochuo sent his minister Mohegan to request that his daughter be given in marriage to the Crown Prince's son.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on xinyou, the Türk khagan Mochuo sent his minister Mohegan to request that his daughter marry the Crown Prince's son.

sentences.zh: 寧州大水，溺殺二千餘人。

translations.literal: Ning Prefecture suffered great floods; more than two thousand people were drowned and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Great floods struck Ning Prefecture, drowning more than two thousand people.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸卯，以正諫大夫朱敬則同平章事。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on guimao, Zhengjian Grandee Zhu Jingze was made Associate Counselor of State.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on guimao, Zhu Jingze, Grandee for Direct Remonstrance, was appointed Associate Counselor of State.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以并州牧相王旦爲雍州牧。

translations.literal: On wushen, the Prince of the Vicarious State Dan, Governor of Bing Prefecture, was made Governor of Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Li Dan, Prince of the Vicarious State and Governor of Bing Prefecture, was made Governor of Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以夏官尚書、檢校涼州都督唐休璟同鳳閣鸞臺三品。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Summer Official Minister and Acting Liang Prefecture Military Commissioner Tang Xiujing was made Associate Third-Rank Courtier of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Tang Xiujing, Minister of the Summer Office and Acting Military Commissioner of Liang Prefecture, was appointed Associate Third-Rank Courtier of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.

sentences.zh: 時突騎施酋長烏質勒與西突厥諸部相攻，安西道絶。

translations.literal: At the time the Turgish chieftain Wuzhile and the various tribes of the Western Türks attacked one another, and the route to Anxi was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Turgish chieftain Wuzhile and the Western Türk tribes were at war with each other, cutting off the Anxi route.

sentences.zh: 太后命休璟與諸宰相議其事，頃之，奏上，太后即依其議施行。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager ordered Xiujing and the various Counselors of State to discuss the matter; shortly their memorial was submitted, and the Empress Dowager immediately carried out the plan according to their recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager ordered Xiujing and the chief ministers to discuss the matter. Shortly their memorial came in, and she adopted their plan at once.

sentences.zh: -{後}-十餘日，安西諸州請兵應接，程期一如休璟所畫，太后謂休璟曰：「恨用卿晩！」

translations.literal: More than ten days later, the prefectures of Anxi requested troops for relief; the schedule was exactly as Xiujing had charted. The Empress Dowager said to Xiujing, "I regret employing you so late!
translations.idiomatic: More than ten days later the Anxi prefectures requested reinforcements, on exactly the schedule Xiujing had drawn up. The Empress Dowager told Xiujing, "I regret putting you in place so late!

sentences.zh: 謂諸宰相曰：「休璟練習邊事，卿曹十不當一。」

translations.literal: She said to the various Counselors of State, "Xiujing is practiced in frontier affairs; the ten of you are not equal to one of him."
translations.idiomatic: She told the ministers, "Xiujing knows the frontier inside out—none of you are worth one of him."

sentences.zh: 時西突厥可汗斛瑟羅用刑殘酷，諸部不服。

translations.literal: At the time the Western Türk qaghan Husheluo's use of punishments was cruel and harsh; the various tribes would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Western Türk qaghan Husheluo punished with cruel severity, and the tribes would not submit.

sentences.zh: 烏質勒本隸斛瑟羅，號莫賀達干，能撫其眾，諸部歸之，斛瑟羅不能制。

translations.literal: Wuzhile had originally been subordinate to Husheluo; titled Mohedagan, he could soothe his people, and the various tribes attached themselves to him—Husheluo could not control him.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhile had originally served under Husheluo. Styled Mohedagan, he knew how to win his people over, and the tribes rallied to him until Husheluo could no longer control him.

sentences.zh: 烏質勒置都督二十員，各將兵七千人，屯碎葉西北；

translations.literal: Wuzhile established twenty commissioners, each leading seven thousand troops, encamped northwest of Suyab;
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhile set up twenty commissioners, each commanding seven thousand men, and encamped northwest of Suyab;

sentences.zh: -{後}-攻陷碎葉，徙其牙帳居之。

translations.literal: Later he attacked and captured Suyab and moved his royal tent to dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: Later he took Suyab and moved his royal encampment there.

sentences.zh: 斛瑟羅部眾離散，因入朝，不敢復還，烏質勒悉並其地。

translations.literal: Husheluo's tribes and followers scattered; he therefore entered court and dared not return again, and Wuzhile annexed all his territory.
translations.idiomatic: Husheluo's followers scattered. He came to court and dared not return, and Wuzhile annexed all his lands.

sentences.zh: 九月，庚寅朔，日有食之，既。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the first day of gengyin, there was an eclipse of the sun—a total eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the first day of gengyin, there was a total eclipse of the sun.

sentences.zh: 初，左台大夫、同鳳閣鸞臺三品魏元忠爲洛州長史，洛陽令張昌儀恃諸兄之勢，每牙，直上長史聽事；

translations.literal: Earlier, Left Platform Grandee and Associate Third-Rank Courtier of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace Wei Yuanzhong served as Luozhou Chief Administrator. Luoyang Magistrate Zhang Changyi relied on his elder brothers' power; on each court day he went straight up to the chief administrator's audience hall;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wei Yuanzhong, Left Platform Grandee and Associate Third-Rank Courtier, served as Chief Administrator of Luozhou. Luoyang Magistrate Zhang Changyi, trading on his brothers' influence, would on court days march straight into the chief administrator's hall;

sentences.zh: 元忠到官，叱下之。

translations.literal: When Yuanzhong took office, he shouted at him and had him removed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanzhong took office, he ordered him down and threw him out.

sentences.zh: 張易之奴暴亂都市，元忠杖殺之。

translations.literal: Zhang Yizhi's slave ran riot in the marketplace; Yuanzhong had him beaten to death with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: A slave of Zhang Yizhi ran riot in the markets, and Yuanzhong had him beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 及爲相，太后召易之弟岐州刺史昌期，欲以爲雍州長史，對仗，問宰相曰：「誰堪雍州者？」

translations.literal: When he became Counselor of State, the Empress Dowager summoned Yizhi's younger brother Changqi, Prefect of Qi Prefecture, intending to make him Chief Administrator of Yong Prefecture. Facing the court formation, she asked the Counselors of State, "Who is fit for Yong Prefecture?
translations.idiomatic: When he became a chief minister, the Empress Dowager summoned Yizhi's brother Changqi, Prefect of Qi Prefecture, intending to appoint him Chief Administrator of Yong Prefecture. In formal audience she asked the ministers, "Who is fit to administer Yong Prefecture?

sentences.zh: 元忠對曰：「今之朝臣無以易薛季昶。」

translations.literal: Yuanzhong replied, "Among the court ministers of today, none can replace Xue Jichang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong replied, "None among today's court ministers can match Xue Jichang.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「季昶久任京府，朕欲別除一官；

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said, "Jichang has long served in the capital districts; We wish to assign him to another office;
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "Jichang has served long in the capital districts. I wish to give him another appointment;

sentences.zh: 昌期何如？」

translations.literal: what of Changqi?"
translations.idiomatic: what about Changqi?"

sentences.zh: 諸相皆曰：「陛下得人矣。」

translations.literal: All the Counselors said, "Your Majesty has found the right man."
translations.idiomatic: All the ministers said, "Your Majesty has found the right man."

sentences.zh: 元忠獨曰：「昌期不堪！」

translations.literal: Yuanzhong alone said, "Changqi is not up to it!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong alone said, "Changqi is not up to the job!"

sentences.zh: 太后問其故，元忠曰：「昌期少年，不閒吏事，向在岐州，戸口逃亡且盡。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager asked the reason. Yuanzhong said, "Changqi is young and unskilled in administrative affairs; when he was in Qi Prefecture, the registered households fled until nearly none remained.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager asked why, Yuanzhong said, "Changqi is young and knows nothing of administration. In Qi Prefecture the registered population fled until nearly none remained.

sentences.zh: 雍州帝京，事務繁劇，不若季昶強幹習事。」

translations.literal: Yong Prefecture is the Imperial Capital; its affairs are numerous and pressing—not like Jichang, strong and capable and practiced in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Prefecture is the imperial capital. Its business is heavy and urgent. Jichang is strong, capable, and experienced in affairs—Changqi is not his equal.

sentences.zh: 太后默然而止。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager fell silent and let the matter drop.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager fell silent and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 元忠又嘗面奏：「臣自先帝以來，蒙被恩渥，今承乏宰相，不能盡忠死節，使小人在側，臣之罪也！」

translations.literal: Yuanzhong also once memorialized to her face: "From the late Emperor until now I have received generous favor; today I hold a Counselor's post in default and cannot exhaust loyalty unto death, yet petty men remain at Your Majesty's side—this is my crime!
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong also once addressed her directly: "Since the late Emperor's day I have enjoyed your favor. Now I hold a chief minister's post I do not deserve, yet I cannot serve you unto death while petty men stand at your side. That is my failing!

sentences.zh: 太后不悅，由是諸張深怨之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was displeased; from this the various Zhangs deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager was displeased, and from then on the Zhang faction deeply resented him.

sentences.zh: 司禮丞高戩，太平公主之所愛也。

translations.literal: Director of Ceremonial Attendant Gao Jian was one whom Princess Taiping favored.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jian, Director of Ceremonial Attendant, was a favorite of Princess Taiping.

sentences.zh: 會太后不豫，張昌宗恐太后一日晏駕，爲元忠所誅，乃譖元忠與戩私議云「太后老矣，不若挾太子爲久長。」

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager fell ill, Zhang Changzong feared that when the Empress Dowager one day passed away he would be executed by Yuanzhong; he therefore slandered Yuanzhong and Jian, saying they had privately discussed: "The Empress Dowager is old; it would be better to rely on the Crown Prince for long-lasting security.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager fell ill, Zhang Changzong feared that after her death Yuanzhong would have him executed, so he slandered Yuanzhong and Jian, claiming they had privately said, "The Empress Dowager is old. Better to rely on the Crown Prince for the long term.

sentences.zh: 太后怒，下元忠、戩獄，將使與昌宗廷辨之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was angry and sent Yuanzhong and Jian to prison, intending to have them dispute the matter with Changzong in court.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager was furious. She imprisoned Yuanzhong and Jian and planned to have them confront Changzong in open court.

sentences.zh: 昌宗密引鳳閣舍人張説，賂以美官，使證元忠，説許之。

translations.literal: Changzong secretly brought in Phoenix Pavilion Secretariat Officer Zhang Yue, bribed him with a fine office, and had him testify against Yuanzhong; Yue agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Changzong secretly summoned Zhang Yue, a Phoenix Pavilion secretariat officer, offered him a splendid appointment to testify against Yuanzhong, and Yue agreed.

sentences.zh: 明日，太后召太子、相王及諸宰相，使元忠與昌宗參對，往復不決。

translations.literal: The next day the Empress Dowager summoned the Crown Prince, the Prince of the Vicarious State, and the various Counselors of State, and had Yuanzhong and Changzong answer each other in turn; back and forth no decision was reached.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Empress Dowager summoned the Crown Prince, the Prince of the Vicarious State, and the chief ministers, and had Yuanzhong and Changzong confront each other. After repeated exchanges nothing was resolved.

sentences.zh: 昌宗曰：「張説聞元忠言，請召問之。」

translations.literal: Changzong said, "Zhang Yue heard Yuanzhong's words—please summon and question him."
translations.idiomatic: Changzong said, "Zhang Yue heard what Yuanzhong said. Summon him and ask."

sentences.zh: 太后召説。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager summoned Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager summoned Zhang Yue.

sentences.zh: 説將入，鳳閣舍人南和宋璟謂説曰：「名義至重，鬼神難欺，不可黨邪陷正以求苟免。

translations.literal: As Yue was about to enter, Phoenix Pavilion Secretariat Officer Song Jing of Nanhe said to Yue, "Righteous reputation is supremely weighty; the spirits of heaven and earth are not to be deceived—you must not band with the wicked to entrap the upright to seek a cheap escape.
translations.idiomatic: As Yue was about to go in, Song Jing of Nanhe, a Phoenix Pavilion secretariat officer, told him, "Honor is everything. The gods cannot be deceived. Do not side with wicked men to frame the upright just to save yourself.

sentences.zh: 若獲罪流竄，其榮多矣。

translations.literal: If you incur guilt and are banished in exile, the glory in that is great indeed.
translations.idiomatic: If you are punished and sent into exile, you will still have glory enough.

sentences.zh: 若事有不測，璟當叩閣力爭，與子同死。

translations.literal: If events take an unforeseen turn, Jing will knock on the palace gates and strive with all his strength, and die with you.
translations.idiomatic: If matters take a bad turn, I will knock on the palace gates and fight for you—and die with you.

sentences.zh: 努力爲之，萬代瞻仰，在此舉也！」

translations.literal: Make a strenuous effort in this matter—ten thousand generations will look up in admiration; it all depends on this one act!
translations.idiomatic: Do your utmost. Ten thousand generations will look to this act—everything hangs on what you do now!

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史濟源張廷珪曰：「朝聞道，夕死可矣！」

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Censor Zhang Tinggui of Jiyuan said, "If one hears the Way in the morning, one may die in the evening!
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Censor Zhang Tinggui of Jiyuan said, "If I have heard the Way this morning, I can die tonight content!

sentences.zh: 左史劉知幾曰：「無污青史，爲子孫累！」

translations.literal: Left Scribe Liu Zhiji said, "Do not stain the blue annals and become a burden on your descendants!"
translations.idiomatic: Left Scribe Liu Zhiji said, "Do not stain the historical record and burden your descendants!"

sentences.zh: 及入，太后問之，説未對。
