translations.literal: When he entered, the Empress Dowager questioned him; Yue did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside, the Empress Dowager questioned him. Yue did not reply.

sentences.zh: 元忠懼，謂説曰：「張説欲與昌宗共羅織魏元忠邪！」

translations.literal: Yuanzhong was afraid and said to Yue, "Does Zhang Yue intend to join with Changzong in fabricating charges against Wei Yuanzhong!
translations.idiomatic: Afraid, Yuanzhong said to Yue, "Are you going to join Changzong in framing Wei Yuanzhong?

sentences.zh: 説叱之曰：「元忠爲宰相，何乃效委巷小人之言！」

translations.literal: Yue rebuked him, saying, "Yuanzhong is a Counselor of State—why do you imitate the talk of back-alley petty men!
translations.idiomatic: Yue snapped at him, "You are a chief minister—why talk like some alleyway gossip?

sentences.zh: 昌宗從旁迫趣説，使速言。

translations.literal: Changzong from the side pressed and urged Yue to speak quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Changzong pressed him from the side, urging him to speak quickly.

sentences.zh: 説曰：「陛下視之，在陛下前，猶逼臣如是，況在外乎！

translations.literal: Yue said, "Your Majesty observes: before Your Majesty he still presses me like this—how much more so outside!
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "Your Majesty sees—even before you he presses me like this. What must he do outside?

sentences.zh: 臣今對廣朝，不敢不以實對。

translations.literal: Your servant now faces the broad court and dares not answer otherwise than with the truth.
translations.idiomatic: I stand now before the full court and dare not answer with anything but the truth.

sentences.zh: 臣實不聞元忠有是言，但昌宗逼臣使誣證之耳！」

translations.literal: Your servant truly did not hear Yuanzhong say such words; it is only that Changzong pressed Your servant to bear false witness against him!
translations.idiomatic: I never heard Yuanzhong say any such thing. Changzong only pressed me to testify falsely against him!

sentences.zh: 易之、昌宗遽呼曰：「張説與魏元忠同反！」

translations.literal: Yizhi and Changzong at once shouted, "Zhang Yue and Wei Yuanzhong rebel together!
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi and Changzong cried out at once, "Zhang Yue and Wei Yuanzhong are plotting rebellion together!

sentences.zh: 太后問其狀。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager asked how this was so.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager asked what they meant.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「説嘗謂元忠爲伊、周；

translations.literal: They replied, "Yue once called Yuanzhong Yi and Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "Yue once compared Yuanzhong to Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou;

sentences.zh: 伊尹放太甲，周公攝王位，非欲反而何？」

translations.literal: Yi Yin deposed Tai Jia, and the Duke of Zhou acted as regent on the throne—if not intending rebellion, what then?
translations.idiomatic: Yi Yin deposed Tai Jia and the Duke of Zhou held the throne as regent—what is that if not rebellion?

sentences.zh: 説曰：「易之兄弟小人，徒聞伊、周之語，安知伊、周之道！

translations.literal: Yue said, "The brothers Yizhi are petty men who have merely heard the words 'Yi and Zhou'—how would they know the Way of Yi and Zhou!
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "The Yizhi brothers are petty men who have heard the names Yi and Zhou—what do they know of what those men stood for?

sentences.zh: 日者元忠初衣紫，臣以郎官往賀，元忠語客曰：『無功受龐，不勝慚懼。』

translations.literal: Recently when Yuanzhong first donned purple robes, Your servant went as a palace gentleman to congratulate him. Yuanzhong spoke to his guests, saying, 'Receiving such largesse without merit, I cannot bear the shame and fear.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanzhong first received the purple robes of office, I went as a palace gentleman to congratulate him. Yuanzhong told his guests, 'I have received great favor without merit. I am ashamed and afraid.

sentences.zh: 臣實言曰：『明公居伊、周之任，何愧三品！』

translations.literal: Your servant truly said, 'Illustrious Sir holds the charge of Yi and Zhou—what shame in the third rank!
translations.idiomatic: I truly said to him, 'You hold the office of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou—what shame is there in a third-rank post?

sentences.zh: 彼伊尹、周公皆爲臣至忠，古今慕仰。

translations.literal: Those Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou were both ministers of utmost loyalty, admired through ancient and modern times.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou were the most loyal of ministers, admired in every age.

sentences.zh: 陛下用宰相，不使學伊、周，當使學誰邪？

translations.literal: When Your Majesty employs Counselors of State, if you do not have them emulate Yi and Zhou, whom should they emulate!
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty appoints chief ministers and does not want them to model Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou, whom should they model?

sentences.zh: 且臣豈不知今日附昌宗立取台衡，附元忠立致族滅！

translations.literal: Moreover, does Your servant not know that today, if one attaches to Changzong one immediately wins the highest post, and if one attaches to Yuanzhong one immediately brings extermination on one's clan!
translations.idiomatic: And do I not know that siding with Changzong wins the highest office at once, while siding with Yuanzhong brings ruin on one's whole clan?

sentences.zh: 但臣畏元忠冤魂，不敢誣之耳。」

translations.literal: Yet Your servant fears Yuanzhong's wronged spirit and dares not bear false witness against him.
translations.idiomatic: But I fear Yuanzhong's wronged ghost, and I dare not testify falsely against him.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「張説反覆小人，宜並系治之。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said, "Zhang Yue is a fickle petty man—he should be imprisoned and investigated together with the others.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "Zhang Yue is an untrustworthy little man. He should be imprisoned along with the rest.

sentences.zh: 他日，更引問，説對如前。

translations.literal: Another day she summoned and questioned him again; Yue answered as before.
translations.idiomatic: Later she questioned him again, and Yue answered as before.

sentences.zh: 太后怒，命宰相與河內王武懿宗共鞫之，説所執如初。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was angry and ordered the Counselors of State and Prince Wu Yizong of Henan jointly to interrogate him; Yue held to his original position.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager was furious and ordered the chief ministers and Wu Yizong, Prince of Henan, to interrogate him together. Yue held firm as before.

sentences.zh: 朱敬則抗疏理之曰：「元忠素稱忠正，張説所坐無名，若令抵罪，失天下望。」

translations.literal: Zhu Jingze submitted a forthright memorial in their defense, saying, "Yuanzhong has long been known as loyal and upright; the charge against Zhang Yue has no name—if they are made to pay for crimes, the hope of the realm will be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jingze submitted a bold memorial in their defense: "Yuanzhong has long been known for loyalty and uprightness. Zhang Yue is charged with nothing real. If you punish them, you will lose the realm's trust.

sentences.zh: 蘇安恆亦上疏，以爲：「陛下革命之初，人以爲納諫之主；

translations.literal: Su Anheng also submitted a memorial, stating, "At the beginning of Your Majesty's revolution, people regarded you as a ruler who accepted remonstrance;
translations.idiomatic: Su Anheng also memorialized, saying, "At the start of your revolution people thought you a ruler who welcomed counsel;

sentences.zh: 暮年以來，人以爲受佞之主。

translations.literal: in the declining years people have come to regard you as a ruler who accepts sycophants.
translations.idiomatic: in your later years they think you a ruler who indulges flatterers.

sentences.zh: 自元忠下獄，里巷恟恟，皆以爲陛下委信奸宄，斥逐賢良。

translations.literal: Since Yuanzhong was imprisoned, the lanes and alleys have been in uproar, all believing that Your Majesty has entrusted authority to treacherous villains and driven away the worthy and good.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yuanzhong's imprisonment the streets have buzzed with fear. People believe you have put traitors in power and driven away the worthy.

sentences.zh: 忠臣烈士，皆撫髀於私室而鉗口於公朝，畏迕易之等意，徒取死而無益。

translations.literal: Loyal ministers and ardent martyrs all strike their thighs in private chambers and clamp their mouths in open court, fearing to contravene Yizhi and the others' intent—only to meet death without benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal men strike their thighs in private and seal their lips in court, afraid to cross Yizhi and his faction. They know protest would mean death for nothing.

sentences.zh: 方今賦役煩重，百姓凋弊，重以讒慝專恣，刑賞失中，竊恐人心不安，別生它變，爭鋒於朱雀門內，問鼎於大明殿前，陛下將何以謝之，何以御之？」

translations.literal: At present levies and corvée are onerous, the common people are depleted and ruined, and on top of this slanderous villains act with arbitrary license while punishments and rewards miss the mark. I secretly fear that hearts are not at peace and other changes will arise—clashing swords within the Vermilion Bird Gate, asking who holds the sacred tripod before the Great Brilliance Hall: how will Your Majesty answer this, how will you control it?
translations.idiomatic: Levies and labor service weigh heavy. The people are exhausted. Slanderers run unchecked, and punishments and rewards have lost their balance. I fear hearts will turn and trouble follow—blades drawn inside the Vermilion Bird Gate and contenders before the Great Brilliance Hall. How will you answer them? How will you hold the throne?

sentences.zh: 易之等見其疏，大怒，欲殺之，賴朱敬則及鳳閣舍人桓彥范、著作郎陸澤魏知古保救得免。

translations.literal: Yizhi and the others saw his memorial, were greatly angered, and wished to kill him; thanks to Zhu Jingze and Phoenix Pavilion Secretariat Officer Huan Yanfan, Compiler Lu Ze, and Wei Zhigu coming to his rescue, he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When Yizhi and his allies read the memorial they wanted Su Anheng killed, but Zhu Jingze, Huan Yanfan, Lu Ze, and Wei Zhigu intervened and saved him.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，貶元忠爲高要尉，戩、説皆流嶺表。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Yuanzhong was demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Gaoyao; Jian and Yue were both banished beyond the Ling Range.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Yuanzhong was demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Gaoyao, while Jian and Yue were both exiled to the far south beyond the Ling Range.

sentences.zh: 元忠辭日，言於太后曰：「臣老矣，今向嶺南，十死一生。

translations.literal: On the day Yuanzhong took leave, he said to the Empress Dowager, "Your servant is old. Now heading south of the Ling Range, it is ten deaths to one life.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he departed, Yuanzhong told the Empress Dowager, "I am old. Going south of the mountains now, I may have one life in ten.

sentences.zh: 陛下他日必有思臣之時。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty will surely one day have occasion to think of Your servant.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty will surely one day remember me.

sentences.zh: 太后問其故，時易之、昌宗皆侍側，元忠指之曰：「此二小兒，終爲亂階。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager asked the reason. At the time Yizhi and Changzong were both attending at her side; Yuanzhong pointed at them and said, "These two children will ultimately become the source of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager asked why, Yizhi and Changzong were beside her. Yuanzhong pointed at them and said, "These two boys will yet bring ruin.

sentences.zh: 易之等下殿，叩膺自擲稱冤。

translations.literal: Yizhi and the others left the hall, beat their breasts and threw themselves about, proclaiming their innocence.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi and his brother left the hall, beating their chests and protesting their innocence.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「元忠去矣！」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said, "Yuanzhong is gone!"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "Yuanzhong is gone!"

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史景城王晙復奏申理元忠，宋璟謂之曰：「魏公幸已得全，今子復冒威怒，得無狼狽乎！」

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Censor Wang Jun of Jingcheng again memorialized to plead Yuanzhong's case. Song Jing said to him, "Duke Wei has fortunately been spared intact; now you again brave the imperial wrath—will you not be caught in disorder!
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Censor Wang Jun of Jingcheng memorialized again to defend Yuanzhong. Song Jing told him, "Wei has barely escaped with his life. If you provoke the Empress Dowager again, will you not come to grief?

sentences.zh: 晙曰：「魏公以忠獲罪，晙爲義所激，顛沛無恨。」

translations.literal: Jun said, "Duke Wei received punishment on account of loyalty; Jun is stirred by righteousness—in confusion and hardship he has no regret.
translations.idiomatic: Jun replied, "Wei was punished for loyalty. I am moved by duty. Even if I suffer for it, I have no regret.

sentences.zh: 璟歎曰：「璟不能申魏公之枉，深負朝廷矣！」

translations.literal: Jing sighed and said, "Jing cannot right Duke Wei's wrong—deeply have I failed the court!"
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing sighed, "I could not clear Wei's name. I have failed the court."

sentences.zh: 太子僕崔貞慎等八人餞元忠於郊外，易之詐爲告密人柴明狀，稱貞慎等與元忠謀反。

translations.literal: Palace Steward Cui Zhenshen and seven others saw Yuanzhong off at the suburbs; Yizhi forged a denunciation as the informer Chai Ming, claiming that Zhenshen and the others plotted rebellion with Yuanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Eight men including Palace Steward Cui Zhenshen saw Yuanzhong off outside the city. Yizhi forged a denunciation in the name of the informant Chai Ming, accusing Zhenshen and the others of plotting rebellion with Yuanzhong.

sentences.zh: 太后使監察御史丹徒馬懷素鞫之，謂懷素曰：「茲事皆實，略問，速以聞。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager sent Investigating Censor Ma Huaisu of Dantu to interrogate them and said to Huaisu, "This affair is all true—question briefly and report quickly.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager sent Investigating Censor Ma Huaisu of Dantu to investigate and told him, "These charges are all true. Question them briefly and report at once.

sentences.zh: 頃之，中使督趣者數四，曰：「反狀皎然，何稽留如此？」

translations.literal: Shortly palace envoys urging haste came four or five times, saying, "The evidence of rebellion is clear—why delay like this?
translations.idiomatic: Soon palace envoys hurried him four or five times, saying, "The evidence of rebellion is clear. Why are you dragging your feet?

sentences.zh: 懷素請柴明對質，太后曰：「我自不知柴明處，但據狀鞫之，安用告者？」

translations.literal: Huaisu requested that Chai Ming be brought to confront them. The Empress Dowager said, "We Ourself do not know Chai Ming's whereabouts—merely interrogate according to the denunciation; what need of the accuser?
translations.idiomatic: Huaisu asked to confront Chai Ming. The Empress Dowager said, "I do not even know where Chai Ming is. Interrogate according to the denunciation. Why need the accuser?

sentences.zh: 懷素據實以聞，太后怒曰：「卿欲縱反者邪？」

translations.literal: Huaisu reported according to the facts. The Empress Dowager was angry and said, "Do you wish to release rebels!
translations.idiomatic: Huaisu reported the facts as he found them. The Empress Dowager snapped, "Do you mean to let rebels go free?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣不敢縱反者。

translations.literal: He replied, "Your servant dares not release rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I would never release rebels.

sentences.zh: 元忠以宰相謫官，貞慎等以親故追送，若誣以爲反，臣實不敢。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong was demoted from the post of Counselor; Zhenshen and the others followed to send him off on account of personal ties—if they are falsely charged as rebels, Your servant truly dares not.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong was demoted from his minister's post. Zhenshen and the others were seeing off a friend. I dare not call that rebellion.

sentences.zh: 昔欒布奏事彭越頭下，漢祖不以爲罪，況元忠之刑未如彭越，而陛下欲誅其送者乎！

translations.literal: Formerly Luan Bu memorialized below Peng Yue's severed head, and Emperor Gaozu of Han did not regard it as a crime—how much more when Yuanzhong's punishment has not reached Peng Yue's level, yet Your Majesty wishes to execute those who saw him off!
translations.idiomatic: When Luan Bu spoke at Peng Yue's severed head, Emperor Gaozu of Han did not treat it as a crime. Yuanzhong's punishment falls far short of Peng Yue's—yet you would execute the men who saw him off?

sentences.zh: 且陛下操生殺之柄，欲加之罪，取決聖衷可矣；

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty holds the power of life and death; if you wish to assign guilt, let the decision come from the imperial heart alone;
translations.idiomatic: And you hold the power of life and death. If you wish to assign guilt, you may decide from your own heart alone;

sentences.zh: 若命臣推鞫，臣敢不以實聞！」

translations.literal: if you charge Your servant to investigate and interrogate, Your servant dares not report other than according to the facts!
translations.idiomatic: but if you order me to investigate, I dare report only what is true!

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「汝欲全不罪邪？」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said, "Do you wish to absolve them entirely of guilt!
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "Do you mean to acquit them entirely?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣智識愚淺，實不見其罪！」

translations.literal: He replied, "Your servant's wisdom and knowledge are shallow and dull—I truly do not see their crime!
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I am too dull to see any crime in what they did!

sentences.zh: 太后意解。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager's anger eased.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager relented.

sentences.zh: 貞慎等由是獲免。

translations.literal: Zhenshen and the others thereby escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenshen and the others were spared.

sentences.zh: 太后嘗命朝貴宴集，易之兄弟皆位在宋璟上。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager once ordered eminent courtiers to assemble for a banquet; Yizhi's brothers all ranked above Song Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager once ordered a banquet for high courtiers. The Yizhi brothers all sat above Song Jing.

sentences.zh: 易之素憚璟，欲悅其意，虛位揖之曰：「公方今第一人，何乃下坐？」

translations.literal: Yizhi had always stood in awe of Jing and wished to please him; he yielded his seat and bowed to him, saying, "Sir, you are the foremost man of today—why sit below?
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi had always feared Song Jing and wanted to win him over. He vacated his seat and bowed, saying, "You are the foremost man in court today. Why sit below me?

sentences.zh: 璟曰：「才劣位卑，張卿以爲第一，何也？」

translations.literal: Jing said, "Talent inferior, rank low—yet Master Zhang holds me the foremost man; why?
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing said, "My talent is modest and my rank is low. Zhang, you call me foremost—why?

sentences.zh: 天官侍郎鄭杲謂璟曰：「中丞奈何卿五郎？」

translations.literal: Heavenly Official Vice Minister Zheng Gao said to Jing, "Imperial Censor, why do you 'sir' the Fifth Master?
translations.idiomatic: Heavenly Official Vice Minister Zheng Gao told Song Jing, "Imperial Censor, why are you using 'sir' on the Fifth Master?

sentences.zh: 璟曰：「以官言之，正當爲卿。

translations.literal: Jing said, "By office speaking, properly one ought to address you as Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing said, "By rank, I ought properly to address you as Minister.

sentences.zh: 足下非張卿家奴，何郎之有！」

translations.literal: Your foot not Zhang Minister's household slave—what young master is there!
translations.idiomatic: You are not a household slave of Master Zhang—what young master could there be!

sentences.zh: 舉坐悚惕。

translations.literal: All seated were fearful and wary.
translations.idiomatic: The entire assembly sat in fear and unease.

sentences.zh: 時自武三思以下，皆謹事易之兄弟，璟獨不爲之禮。

translations.literal: At the time from Wu Sansi below, all carefully attended the Yizhi brothers; Jing alone did not perform ritual toward them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, everyone from Wu Sansi down treated the Yizhi brothers with deferential care, but Song Jing alone refused to show them courtesy.

sentences.zh: 諸張積怒，常欲中傷之；

translations.literal: The various Zhangs accumulated anger, often wishing to strike him by slander;
translations.idiomatic: The Zhang faction nursed deep resentment and often sought to harm him by slander;

sentences.zh: 太后知之，故得免。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager knew this; therefore he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager knew of it, and so he was spared.

sentences.zh: 丁未，以左武衞大將軍武攸宜充西京留守。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Left Martial Guard Grand General Wu Youyi was appointed to serve as Western Capital Regent.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Wu Youyi, Grand General of the Left Martial Guard, was appointed Regent of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙寅，車駕發西京；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on bingyin, the imperial carriage set out from the Western Capital;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on bingyin, the imperial carriage departed the Western Capital;

sentences.zh: 乙酉，至神都。

translations.literal: On yiyou, it arrived at Shendu.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, it reached Shendu.

sentences.zh: 十一月，己丑，突厥遣使謝許昏。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jichou, the Turks sent envoys to thank them for the promised marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jichou, the Turks sent envoys to express gratitude for the promised marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 丙申，宴於宿羽台，太子預焉。

translations.literal: On bingshen, a banquet was held at Suyu Terrace; the Crown Prince participated therein.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, a banquet was held at Suyu Terrace, and the Crown Prince was present.

sentences.zh: 宮尹崔神慶上疏，以爲：「今五品以上所以佩龜者，爲別敕徵召，恐有詐妄，內出龜合，然-{後}-應命。

translations.literal: Palace Intendant Cui Shenqing submitted a memorial, stating, "The reason officials of the fifth rank and above wear tortoise badges is so that when specially summoned by separate edict, for fear of fraud, the palace issues the tortoise tally and only then may one respond to the order.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Intendant Cui Shenqing submitted a memorial stating, "Officials of the fifth rank and above wear tortoise badges so that when they are specially summoned by edict, the palace can issue the tortoise tally from within before they respond—this guards against fraud.

sentences.zh: 況太子國本，古來徵召皆用玉契。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Crown Prince is the nation's foundation; since antiquity summons have all used jade tallies.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Crown Prince is the foundation of the realm; since antiquity, summons have always used jade tallies.

sentences.zh: 此誠重慎之極也。

translations.literal: This is truly the extreme of heavy caution.
translations.idiomatic: This is indeed the very height of prudent caution.

sentences.zh: 昨緣突厥使見，太子應預朝參，直有文符下宮，曾不降敕處分，臣愚謂太子非朔望朝參、應別召者，望降墨敕及玉契。」

translations.literal: Yesterday, because the Turkish envoys were received, the Crown Prince ought to have attended court audience, yet only a routine document was sent down to the palace with no issued edict of appointment. In my humble view, when the Crown Prince is not attending the new- and full-moon audiences but is to be specially summoned, I hope Your Majesty will issue a black-ink edict and a jade tally.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday, because the Turkish envoys were received, the Crown Prince should have attended court, yet only a routine document was sent to the palace with no edict of appointment. In my humble view, whenever the Crown Prince is summoned outside the regular new- and full-moon audiences, I hope Your Majesty will issue a black-ink edict and a jade tally.

sentences.zh: 太后甚然之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager greatly agreed with this.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager strongly approved.

sentences.zh: 始安獠歐陽倩擁眾數萬，攻陷州縣，朝廷思得良吏以鎮之。

translations.literal: The Shi'an Liao Ouyang Qian gathered a host of tens of thousands, attacked and captured prefectures and counties; the court wished to obtain a good official to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Qian, a Liao chieftain in Shi'an, gathered a force of tens of thousands, attacked and seized prefectures and counties. The court sought a capable official to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 朱敬則稱司封郎中裴懷古有文武才；

translations.literal: Zhu Jingze commended Si Feng Director Pei Huaigu as having both civil and military talent;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jingze recommended Pei Huaigu, a Director in the Bureau of Appointments, as a man of both civil and military talent;

sentences.zh: 制以懷古爲桂州都督，仍充招慰討擊使。

translations.literal: An edict made Huaigu Military Commissioner of Gui Prefecture and additionally appointed him Pacification and Attack Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Huaigu Military Commissioner of Gui Prefecture and also appointed him Pacification and Attack Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 懷古才及嶺上，飛書示以禍福，倩等迎降，且言「爲吏所侵逼，故舉兵自救耳。」

translations.literal: Huaigu had only just reached the mountains when he sent flying letters showing fortune and misfortune; Qian and the others came out to surrender, saying also, "We were oppressed by officials and therefore raised troops to save ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Huaigu had only just crossed the mountains when he sent urgent letters explaining the consequences of resistance or submission. Qian and the others came out to surrender, saying, "We were oppressed by officials and therefore raised troops to save ourselves.

sentences.zh: 懷古輕騎赴之。

translations.literal: Huaigu with light cavalry went to them.
translations.idiomatic: Huaigu rode lightly to meet them.

sentences.zh: 左右曰：「夷獠無信，不可忽也。」

translations.literal: Those around him said, "The barbarian Liao are untrustworthy—this cannot be taken lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Those around him said, "The Liao barbarians are untrustworthy—this cannot be taken lightly.

sentences.zh: 懷古曰：「吾仗忠信，可通神明，而況人乎！」

translations.literal: Huaigu said, "I rely on loyalty and trust, which can reach the spirits—how much more so men!
translations.idiomatic: Huaigu said, "I rely on loyalty and trust, which can reach even the spirits—how much more so ordinary men!

sentences.zh: 遂詣其營，賊眾大喜，歸所掠貨財；

translations.literal: He then went to their camp; the rebel host greatly rejoiced and returned their plundered goods;
translations.idiomatic: He then went to their camp. The rebels rejoiced and returned the goods they had seized;

sentences.zh: 諸洞酋長素持兩端者，皆來款附，嶺外悉定。

translations.literal: Cave chieftains who had long hedged their allegiances all came to submit; beyond the mountains all was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Cave chieftains who had long hedged their allegiances all came to submit, and the region beyond the mountains was entirely pacified.

sentences.zh: 是歳，分命使者以六條察州縣。

translations.literal: That year, envoys were separately dispatched to inspect prefectures and counties by the Six Regulations.
translations.idiomatic: That year, envoys were dispatched in separate groups to inspect prefectures and counties under the Six Regulations.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃南境諸部皆叛，贊普器弩悉弄自將擊之，卒於軍中。

translations.literal: All the southern-border tribes of Tibet rebelled; the tsenpo Qinuixinong personally led troops to attack them and died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: All the tribes along Tibet's southern border rebelled. The tsenpo Qinuixinong personally led troops to suppress them and died in camp.

sentences.zh: 諸子爭立，久之，國人立其子棄隸蹜贊爲贊普，生七年矣。

translations.literal: Sons struggled for the throne; after a long time the people enthroned his son Qilizuzan as tsenpo—he was seven years old.
translations.idiomatic: His sons fought over the succession. After a long interval, the people enthroned his son Qilizuzan as tsenpo; he was seven years old.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丙申，冊拜右武衞將軍阿史那懷道爲西突厥十姓可汗。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on bingshen, Ashina Huaidao, General of the Right Martial Guard, was enfeoffed and appointed Qaghan of the Ten Surnames of the Western Turks.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on bingshen, Ashina Huaidao, General of the Right Martial Guard, was enfeoffed and appointed Qaghan of the Ten Surnames of the Western Turks.

sentences.zh: 懷道，斛瑟羅之子也。

translations.literal: Huaidao was the son of Gusuoluo.
translations.idiomatic: Huaidao was the son of Gusuoluo.

sentences.zh: 丁未，毀三陽宮，以其材作興泰宮於萬安山。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Sanyang Palace was demolished and its materials used to build Xingtai Palace on Mount Wan'an.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Sanyang Palace was demolished and its materials used to build Xingtai Palace on Mount Wan'an.

sentences.zh: 二宮皆武三思建議爲之，請太后每歳臨幸，功費甚廣，百姓苦之。

translations.literal: Both palaces were proposed by Wu Sansi; he asked the Empress Dowager to visit each year. The labor and expense were vast, and the people suffered.
translations.idiomatic: Both palaces had been proposed by Wu Sansi, who urged the Empress Dowager to visit them every year. The labor and expense were enormous, and the people suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 左拾遺盧藏用上疏，以爲：「左右近臣多以順意爲忠，朝廷具僚皆以犯忤爲戒，致陛下不知百姓失業，傷陛下之仁。

translations.literal: Left Remonstrating Editorial Assistant Lu Zangyong submitted a memorial, stating, "Near ministers mostly treat compliance as loyalty, while full officials in court all take giving offense as a warning, causing Your Majesty not to know that the people have lost their livelihoods and harming Your Majesty's benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Left Remonstrating Editorial Assistant Lu Zangyong submitted a memorial stating, "Those close to the throne mostly treat compliance as loyalty, while officials throughout the court all treat giving offense as a warning. This keeps Your Majesty from learning that the people have lost their livelihoods and it harms Your Majesty's benevolence.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能以勞人爲辭，發制罷之，則天下皆知陛下苦己而愛人也。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty can sincerely take burdening the people as the reason and issue an edict abolishing them, then all under heaven will know Your Majesty restrains yourself and loves the people.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty can sincerely cite the burden on the people and issue an edict abolishing the project, then all under heaven will know that Your Majesty restrains yourself and loves the people.

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: She did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: She did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 藏用，承慶之弟孫也。

translations.literal: Zangyong was the younger brother's grandson of Chengqing.
translations.idiomatic: Zangyong was the great-nephew of Chengqing.

sentences.zh: 壬子，以天官侍郎韋嗣立爲鳳閣侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On renzi, Tian Guan Vice Minister Wei Sili was made Fengge Vice Minister and Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Wei Sili, Vice Minister of the Bureau of Celestial Offices, was appointed Fengge Vice Minister and Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State.

sentences.zh: 夏官侍郎、同鳳閣鸞臺三品李迥秀頗受賄賂，監察御史馬懷素劾奏之。

translations.literal: Summer Official Vice Minister and Associate Third-Rank Courtier of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace Li Jiaoxiu rather accepted bribes; Investigative Censor Ma Huaisu impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiaoxiu, Summer Official Vice Minister and Associate Third-Rank Courtier of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, had accepted bribes rather freely; Investigative Censor Ma Huaisu impeached him.

sentences.zh: 二月，癸亥，迥秀貶廬州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second month, on guihai, Jiaoxiu was demoted to Prefect of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on guihai, Li Jiaoxiu was demoted to Prefect of Lu.

sentences.zh: 壬申，正諫大夫、同平章事朱敬則以老疾致仕。

translations.literal: On renshen, Zhengjian Grandee and Fellow Assessor Zhu Jingze retired due to age and illness.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Zhu Jingze, Grandee for Direct Remonstrance and Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State, retired because of age and illness.

sentences.zh: 敬則爲相，以用人爲先，自餘細務不之視。

translations.literal: As chancellor, Jingze put selecting men first and did not attend to other minor matters.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor, Zhu Jingze put selecting men first and paid no attention to other minor affairs.

sentences.zh: 太后嘗與宰相議及刺史、縣令。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager once discussed with the chancellors provincial prefects and county magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager once discussed provincial prefects and county magistrates with the chancellors.

sentences.zh: 三月，己丑，李嶠、唐休璟等奏：「竊見朝廷物議，遠近人情，莫不重內官，輕外職，每除授牧伯，皆再三披訴。

translations.literal: In the third month, on jichou, Li Jiao, Tang Xiujing, and others memorialized, "We observe court discussion and sentiment near and far—none do not value inner offices and slight outer posts. Whenever provincial governors are appointed, they repeatedly plead and protest.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jichou, Li Jiao, Tang Xiujing, and others memorialized, "We observe that in court discussion and in sentiment near and far alike, everyone values inner offices and looks down on outer posts. Whenever a provincial governorship is assigned, the appointee repeatedly pleads and protests.

sentences.zh: 比來所遣外任，多是貶累之人；

translations.literal: Recently dispatched outer appointments have mostly been men burdened by demotion;
translations.idiomatic: Recently, those sent to outer posts have mostly been men burdened by demotion;

sentences.zh: 風俗不澄，實由於此。

translations.literal: Customs are not clear—this is truly the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Public morals are not pure—and this is truly the reason.

sentences.zh: 望於台、閣、寺、監妙簡賢良，分典大州，共康庶績。

translations.literal: We hope from the bureaus, halls, directorates, and commissions excellent men will be finely selected to administer great prefectures and together bring prosperity to the people.
translations.idiomatic: We hope that from the bureaus, halls, directorates, and commissions worthy men will be carefully selected to govern great prefectures and together bring prosperity to the people.

sentences.zh: 臣等請輟近侍，率先具僚。」

translations.literal: We your ministers ask to give up near attendance and take the lead among the full officials.
translations.idiomatic: We your ministers ask to give up our posts at court and take the lead among the full officials.

sentences.zh: 太后命書名探之，得韋嗣立及御史大夫楊再思等二十人。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager ordered names written and drawn; she obtained Wei Sili and Censor-in-Chief Yang Zaisi and others, twenty men in all.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager ordered names written and lots drawn, and obtained Wei Sili, Censor-in-Chief Yang Zaisi, and eighteen others—twenty men in all.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，制各以本官檢校刺史，嗣立爲汴州刺史。

translations.literal: On guisi, an edict made each serve in his present office as acting prefect; Sili was made Prefect of Bian.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, an edict made each man serve in his present office as acting prefect; Wei Sili was made Prefect of Bian.

sentences.zh: 其-{後}-政跡可稱者，唯常州刺史薛謙光、徐州刺史司馬金皇而已。

translations.literal: Afterward, those whose governance could be praised were only Chang Prefecture Prefect Xue Qianguang and Xu Prefecture Prefect Sima Jinhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, of those sent out, only Xue Qianguang, Prefect of Chang, and Sima Jinhuang, Prefect of Xu, had records of governance worth praising.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，徙平恩王重福爲譙王。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Prince Ping'en Zhongfu was moved to Prince of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Prince Ping'en Zhongfu was reassigned as Prince of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 以夏官侍郎宗楚客同平章事。

translations.literal: Summer Official Vice Minister Zong Chuke was made Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Chuke, Vice Minister of the Bureau of Summer Offices, was made Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State.

sentences.zh: 鳳閣侍郎、同鳳閣鸞臺三品蘇味道謁歸葬其父，制州縣供葬事。

translations.literal: Fengge Vice Minister and Associate Third-Rank Courtier of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace Su Weidao returned home to bury his father; an edict ordered the prefectures and counties to supply the funeral arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: Su Weidao, Fengge Vice Minister and Associate Third-Rank Courtier of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, returned home to bury his father, and an edict ordered the prefectures and counties to supply the funeral arrangements.

sentences.zh: 味道因之侵毀鄕人墓田，役使過度。

translations.literal: Weidao used this to encroach on and destroy neighbors' grave lands and overused corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: Weidao used the occasion to encroach on and destroy his neighbors' grave lands and to overuse corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 監察御史蕭至忠劾奏之，左遷坊州刺史。

translations.literal: Investigative Censor Xiao Zhizhong impeached him, and he was demoted to Prefect of Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Investigative Censor Xiao Zhizhong impeached him, and he was demoted to Prefect of Fang.

sentences.zh: 至忠，引之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Zhizhong was a great-grandson of Yinzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zhizhong was a great-grandson of Yinzhi.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，壬戌，同鳳閣鸞臺三品韋安石知納言，李嶠知內史事。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on renxu, Associate Third-Rank Courtier of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace Wei Anshi took charge of the Censorate, and Li Jiao took charge of the Inner Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on renxu, Wei Anshi, Associate Third-Rank Courtier of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, took charge of the Censorate, and Li Jiao took charge of the Inner Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太后幸興泰宮。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager visited Xingtai Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager visited Xingtai Palace.

sentences.zh: 太后復稅天下僧尼，作大像於白司馬阪，令春官尚書武攸寧檢校，糜費巨億。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager again levied a tax on Buddhist monks and nuns throughout the empire and had a great statue built at Baima Slope; she put Spring Official Minister Wu Youning in charge of supervision, and the waste ran to hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager again levied a tax on Buddhist monks and nuns throughout the empire and had a great statue built at Baima Slope. She put Wu Youning, Minister of the Bureau of Spring Offices, in charge of supervision, and the waste ran to hundreds of millions.

sentences.zh: 李嶠上疏，以爲：「天下編戸，貧弱者眾。

translations.literal: Li Jiao submitted a memorial, stating, "Registered households throughout the empire include many who are poor and weak.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiao submitted a memorial stating, "Registered households throughout the empire include many who are poor and weak.

sentences.zh: 造像錢見有一十七萬餘緡，若將散施，人與一千，濟得一十七萬餘戸。

translations.literal: Funds for the statue presently amount to more than one hundred and seventy thousand strings of cash; if distributed, giving each person one thousand, one could aid more than one hundred and seventy thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Funds for the statue presently amount to more than one hundred and seventy thousand strings of cash. If distributed at one thousand per person, more than one hundred and seventy thousand households could be helped.

sentences.zh: 拯饑寒之弊，省勞役之勤，順諸佛慈悲之心，沾聖君亭育之意，人神胥悅，功德無窮。

translations.literal: Rescuing the harm of hunger and cold, saving the toil of corvée labor, accorded with the compassionate heart of the Buddhas and touched the nurturing intent of the sage ruler—men and spirits alike would rejoice, and the merit would be boundless.
translations.idiomatic: Relieving hunger and cold, sparing the people corvée toil, honoring the compassionate heart of the Buddhas and fulfilling the nurturing intent of the sage ruler—men and spirits alike would rejoice, and the merit would be boundless.

sentences.zh: 方作過-{後}-因緣，豈如見在果報！」

translations.literal: Making karma for the future—how can that compare with karmic reward in the present!
translations.idiomatic: Building merit for the afterlife—how can that compare with reward in the present life!

sentences.zh: 監察御史張廷珪上疏諫曰：「臣以時政論之，則宜先邊境，蓄府庫，養人力；

translations.literal: Investigative Censor Zhang Tinggui submitted a remonstrance, stating, "From the standpoint of current affairs, one ought first to secure the borders, fill the treasuries, and nurture manpower;
translations.idiomatic: Investigative Censor Zhang Tinggui submitted a remonstrance stating, "From the standpoint of current affairs, one ought first to secure the borders, fill the treasuries, and nurture manpower;

sentences.zh: 以釋教論之，則宜救苦厄，滅諸相，崇無爲。

translations.literal: From the standpoint of Buddhism, one ought to rescue suffering, eliminate all forms, and honor non-action.
translations.idiomatic: From the standpoint of Buddhism, one ought to rescue suffering, eliminate all forms, and honor non-action.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下察臣之愚，行佛之意，務以理爲上，不以人廢言。」

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to discern my folly, act in the spirit of the Buddha, and make reason paramount rather than dismissing words because of the person who speaks them.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to discern my folly, act in the spirit of the Buddha, make reason paramount, and not dismiss words because of the person who speaks them.

sentences.zh: 太后爲之罷役，仍召見廷珪，深賞慰之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager halted the project on this account, and also summoned Tinggui and deeply praised and consoled him.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager halted the project on this account, summoned Tinggui, and deeply praised and consoled him.

sentences.zh: 鳳閣侍郎、同鳳閣鸞臺三品姚元崇以母老固請歸侍；

translations.literal: Fengge Vice Minister and Associate Third-Rank Courtier of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace Yao Yuanchong, because his mother was old, firmly requested to return home to serve her;
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yuanchong, Fengge Vice Minister and Associate Third-Rank Courtier of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, because his mother was old, firmly requested to return home to serve her;

sentences.zh: 六月，辛酉，以元崇行相王府長史，秩位並同三品。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on xinyou, Yuanchong was made provisional Chief Secretary of the Prince of Xiang's household, with rank and position both equal to the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on xinyou, Yao Yuanchong was made provisional Chief Secretary of the Prince of Xiang's household, with rank and position both equal to the third rank.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，以天官侍郎崔玄□同平章事。

translations.literal: On yichou, Tian Guan Vice Minister Cui Xuanwei was made Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Cui Xuanwei, Vice Minister of the Bureau of Celestial Offices, was made Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State.

sentences.zh: 召鳳閣侍郎、同平章事、檢校汴州刺史韋嗣立赴興泰宮。

translations.literal: Wei Sili, Fengge Vice Minister, Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State, and acting Prefect of Bian, was summoned to Xingtai Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sili, Fengge Vice Minister, Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State, and acting Prefect of Bian, was summoned to Xingtai Palace.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，以李嶠同鳳閣鸞臺三品。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Li Jiao was made Associate Third-Rank Courtier of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Li Jiao was made Associate Third-Rank Courtier of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.

sentences.zh: 嶠自請解內史。

translations.literal: Jiao himself requested to resign from the Inner Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiao himself requested to resign from the Inner Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 壬午，以相王府長史姚元崇兼知夏官尚書、同鳳閣鸞臺三品。

translations.literal: On renwu, Yao Yuanchong, provisional Chief Secretary of the Prince of Xiang's household, was additionally made acting Summer Official Minister and Associate Third-Rank Courtier of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, Yao Yuanchong, provisional Chief Secretary of the Prince of Xiang's household, was additionally made acting Minister of the Bureau of Summer Offices and Associate Third-Rank Courtier of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丙戌，以神都副留守楊再思爲內史。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingxu, Yang Zaisi, Deputy Regent of Shendu, was made head of the Inner Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on bingxu, Yang Zaisi, Deputy Regent of Shendu, was made head of the Inner Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 再思爲相，專以諂媚取容。

translations.literal: As chancellor, Zaisi relied solely on flattery to win favor.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor, Yang Zaisi relied solely on flattery to win favor.

sentences.zh: 司禮少卿張同休，易之兄也，嘗召公卿宴集，酒酣，戲再思曰：「楊內史面似高麗。」

translations.literal: Director of Ceremonials Zhang Tongxiu, Yizhi's elder brother, once summoned the chief ministers to a banquet; when the wine had gone deep, he joked to Zaisi, "Minister Yang's face resembles Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Ceremonials Zhang Tongxiu, Zhang Yizhi's elder brother, once summoned the chief ministers to a banquet. When the wine had gone deep, he joked to Yang Zaisi, "Minister Yang's face resembles Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 再思欣然，即剪紙帖巾，反披紫袍，爲高麗舞，舉坐大笑。

translations.literal: Zaisi gladly accepted this, immediately cut paper and pasted it on his headcloth, reversed his purple robe, performed a Goryeo dance, and the whole assembly roared with laughter.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zaisi gladly accepted this, cut paper and pasted it on his headcloth, reversed his purple robe, performed a Goryeo dance, and the whole assembly roared with laughter.

sentences.zh: 時人或譽張昌宗之美曰：「六郎面似蓮花。」

translations.literal: Some at the time praised Zhang Changzong's beauty, saying, "Sixth Master's face is like a lotus.
translations.idiomatic: Some at the time praised Zhang Changzong's beauty, saying, "Sixth Master's face is like a lotus.

sentences.zh: 再思獨曰：「不然。」

translations.literal: Zaisi alone said, "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zaisi alone said, "Not so.

sentences.zh: 昌宗問其故，再思曰：「乃蓮花似六郎耳。」

translations.literal: Changzong asked the reason; Zaisi said, "Rather, it is the lotus that resembles Sixth Master."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Changzong asked the reason. Yang Zaisi said, "Rather, it is the lotus that resembles Sixth Master."

sentences.zh: 甲午，太后還宮。

translations.literal: On jiawu, the Empress Dowager returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, the Empress Dowager returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 乙未，司禮少卿張同休、汴州刺史張昌期、尚方少監張昌儀皆坐贓下獄，命左右台共鞫之；

translations.literal: On yiwei, Director of Ceremonials Zhang Tongxiu, Prefect of Bian Zhang Changqi, and Assistant Director of the Palace Workshops Zhang Changyi were all imprisoned on charges of corruption; the Left and Right Censorates were ordered jointly to interrogate them;
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Zhang Tongxiu, Director of Ceremonials, Zhang Changqi, Prefect of Bian, and Zhang Changyi, Assistant Director of the Palace Workshops, were all imprisoned on charges of corruption, and the Left and Right Censorates were ordered jointly to interrogate them;

sentences.zh: 丙申，敕，張易之、張昌宗作威作福，亦命同鞫。

translations.literal: On bingshen, an edict stated that Zhang Yizhi and Zhang Changzong had abused their power and arrogated blessings to themselves, and they too were ordered interrogated together.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, an edict stated that Zhang Yizhi and Zhang Changzong had abused their power and arrogated blessings to themselves, and they too were ordered interrogated together.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，司刑正賈敬言奏：「張昌宗強市人田，應徵銅二十斤。」

translations.literal: On xinchou, Director of Punishments Jia Jingyan memorialized, "Zhang Changzong forcibly purchased a man's land and should pay a fine of twenty jin of copper.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Jia Jingyan, Director of Punishments, memorialized, "Zhang Changzong forcibly purchased a man's land and should pay a fine of twenty jin of copper.

sentences.zh: 制「可」。

translations.literal: An edict stated, "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated, "Approved."

sentences.zh: 乙巳，御史大夫李承嘉、中丞桓彥范奏：「張同休兄弟贓共四千餘緡，張昌宗法應免官。」

translations.literal: On yisi, Censor-in-Chief Li Chengjia and Vice Censor-in-Chief Huan Yanfan memorialized, "The bribes of Zhang Tongxiu and his brothers together amounted to more than four thousand strings of cash; by law Zhang Changzong should be removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Li Chengjia, Censor-in-Chief, and Huan Yanfan, Vice Censor-in-Chief, memorialized, "The bribes of Zhang Tongxiu and his brothers together amounted to more than four thousand strings of cash. By law Zhang Changzong should be removed from office.

sentences.zh: 昌宗奏：「臣有功於國，所犯不至免官。」

translations.literal: Changzong memorialized, "Your subject has merit to the state; the offense does not reach the level of removal from office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Changzong memorialized, "Your subject has merit to the state; the offense does not reach the level of removal from office.

sentences.zh: 太后問諸宰相：「昌宗有功乎？」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager asked the chancellors, "Does Changzong have merit?
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager asked the chancellors, "Does Changzong have merit?

sentences.zh: 楊再思曰：「昌宗合神丹，聖躬服之有驗，此莫大之功。」

translations.literal: Yang Zaisi said, "Changzong compounded the divine elixir; the Sacred Person took it with effect—this is a merit without equal.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zaisi said, "Changzong compounded the divine elixir. The Sacred Person took it with effect—this is a merit without equal.

sentences.zh: 太后悅，赦昌宗罪，復其官。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was pleased, pardoned Changzong's offense, and restored his office.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager was pleased, pardoned Zhang Changzong's offense, and restored his office.

sentences.zh: 左補闕戴令言作《兩腳狐賦》，以譏再思，再思出令言爲長社令。

translations.literal: Left Supplementation Daim Lingyan composed the rhapsody "Two-Legged Fox" to satirize Zaisi; Zaisi sent Lingyan out as Magistrate of Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: Left Supplementation Daim Lingyan composed the rhapsody "Two-Legged Fox" to satirize Yang Zaisi; Yang Zaisi sent Lingyan out as Magistrate of Changshe.

sentences.zh: 丙午，夏官侍郎、同平章事宗楚客有罪，左遷原州都督，充靈武道行軍大總管。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Summer Official Vice Minister and Fellow Assessor Zong Chuke was found guilty and demoted to Military Commissioner of Yuan Prefecture, serving as Grand Commander of the Lingwu Route Field Army.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Zong Chuke, Vice Minister of the Bureau of Summer Offices and Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State, was found guilty and demoted to Military Commissioner of Yuan Prefecture, serving as Grand Commander of the Lingwu Route Field Army.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，張同休貶岐山丞，張昌儀貶博望丞。

translations.literal: On guichou, Zhang Tongxiu was demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Qishan, and Zhang Changyi was demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Bowang.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Zhang Tongxiu was demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Qishan, and Zhang Changyi was demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Bowang.

sentences.zh: 鸞臺侍郎、知納言事、同鳳閣鸞臺三品韋安石舉奏張易之等罪，敕付安石及右庶子、同鳳閣鸞臺三品唐休璟鞫之，未竟而事變。

translations.literal: Luantai Vice Minister, acting Censor-in-Chief, and Associate Third-Rank Courtier of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace Wei Anshi impeached Zhang Yizhi and the others for their crimes; an edict ordered Anshi and Right Secretariat Assistant and Associate Third-Rank Courtier Tang Xiujing to interrogate them, but before the inquiry was finished the affair changed.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Anshi, Luantai Vice Minister, acting Censor-in-Chief, and Associate Third-Rank Courtier of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, impeached Zhang Yizhi and the others for their crimes. An edict ordered Anshi and Tang Xiujing, Right Secretariat Assistant and Associate Third-Rank Courtier, to interrogate them, but before the inquiry was finished the affair changed.

sentences.zh: 八月，甲寅，以安石兼檢校揚州長史，庚申，以休璟兼幽營都督、安東都護。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on jiayin, Anshi was additionally made acting Chief Secretary of Yang Prefecture; on gengshen, Xiujing was additionally made Military Commissioner of You and Ying and Protector-General of Andong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jiayin, Wei Anshi was additionally made acting Chief Secretary of Yang Prefecture; on gengshen, Tang Xiujing was additionally made Military Commissioner of You and Ying and Protector-General of Andong.

sentences.zh: 休璟將行，密言於太子曰：「二張恃寵不臣，必將之亂。

translations.literal: As Xiujing was about to depart, he secretly spoke to the Crown Prince, "The Two Zhangs rely on favor and are insubordinate—they will surely bring chaos.
translations.idiomatic: As Tang Xiujing was about to depart, he secretly spoke to the Crown Prince, "The Two Zhangs rely on favor and are insubordinate—they will surely bring chaos.

sentences.zh: 殿下宜備之。」

translations.literal: Your Highness ought to prepare.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness ought to prepare.

sentences.zh: 相王府長史兼知夏官尚書事、同鳳閣鸞臺三品姚元崇上言：「臣事相王，不宜典兵馬。

translations.literal: Yao Yuanchong, provisional Chief Secretary of the Prince of Xiang's household, additionally acting Summer Official Minister, and Associate Third-Rank Courtier of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, submitted a statement, "Your subject serves the Prince of Xiang and ought not command troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yuanchong, provisional Chief Secretary of the Prince of Xiang's household, additionally acting Minister of the Bureau of Summer Offices, and Associate Third-Rank Courtier of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, submitted a statement, "Your subject serves the Prince of Xiang and ought not command troops and horses.

sentences.zh: 臣不敢愛死，恐不益於王。」

translations.literal: Your subject does not dare spare my life, for fear it would not benefit the Prince."
translations.idiomatic: I do not dare hold back my life, for fear it would not benefit the Prince."

sentences.zh: 辛酉，改春官尚書，餘如故。

translations.literal: On xinyou, his post was changed to Spring Official Minister; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou he was reassigned as Minister of Spring Offices; his other posts remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 元崇字元之，時突厥叱列元崇反，太后命元崇以字行。

translations.literal: Yuanchong's courtesy name was Yuanzhi. At the time Chilie Yuanchong of the Turks rebelled, so the Empress Dowager ordered Yuanchong to use his courtesy name in official use.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchong's courtesy name was Yuanzhi. When a Turk named Chilie Yuanchong rose in rebellion, the Empress Dowager ordered Yao to go by his courtesy name in office to avoid confusion.

sentences.zh: 突厥默啜既和親，戊寅，始遣淮陽王武延秀還。

translations.literal: After the Turk Mo-chuo had made peace and alliance, on wuyin the Huaiyang Prince Wu Yanxiu was at last sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Turk khan Mo-chuo had agreed to peace and alliance, on wuyin the court at last sent the Prince of Huaiyang, Wu Yanxiu, home.

sentences.zh: 九月，壬子，以姚元之充靈武道行軍大總管；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on renzi, Yao Yuanzhi was appointed Grand Commander of the Lingwu Circuit campaign army;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on renzi, Yao Yuanchong was made Grand Commander of the campaign army on the Lingwu Circuit;

sentences.zh: 辛酉，以元之爲靈武道安撫大使。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Yuanzhi was made Pacification Commissioner for the Lingwu Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou he was appointed Pacification Commissioner for the Lingwu Circuit.

sentences.zh: 元之將行，太后令舉外司堪爲宰相者。

translations.literal: As Yuanzhi was about to depart, the Empress Dowager ordered him to recommend members of the outer service who were fit to serve as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: As Yuanchong prepared to leave, the Empress Dowager told him to nominate suitable men from the outer service for chancellor.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「張柬之沉厚有謀，能斷大事，且其人已老。

translations.literal: He replied, "Zhang Jianzhi is steady and profound and full of strategy; he can decide great matters, and moreover the man is already old.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Zhang Jianzhi is steady, deep, and far-sighted, capable of deciding great affairs; moreover, he is already advanced in years.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下急用之。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should employ him at once."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should put him to use without delay."

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲戌，以秋官侍郎張柬之同平章事，時年且八十矣。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiaxu, Autumn Official Vice Minister Zhang Jianzhi was made Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State; he was then nearly eighty.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on jiaxu, Zhang Jianzhi, Vice Minister of the Bureau of Autumn Offices, was made Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State; he was then nearly eighty.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，以韋嗣立檢校魏州刺史，餘如故。

translations.literal: On yihai, Wei Silai was made acting Prefect of Wei Prefecture; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Wei Silai was appointed acting Prefect of Wei Prefecture; his other posts were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 壬午，以懷州長史河南房融同平章事。

translations.literal: On renwu, Fang Rong of Henan, Chief Secretary of Huai Prefecture, was made Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, Fang Rong of Henan, Chief Secretary of Huai Prefecture, was elevated to Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State.

sentences.zh: 太后命宰相各舉堪爲員外郎者，韋嗣立薦廣武令岑羲曰：「但恨其伯父長倩爲累。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager ordered each chancellor to recommend men fit to serve as assistant department directors. Wei Silai recommended Guangwu Magistrate Cen Xi, saying, "It is only a pity that his uncle Changqian is a burden upon him."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager ordered each chancellor to recommend men suitable for assistant department director. Wei Silai recommended Cen Xi, Magistrate of Guangwu, saying, "My only regret is that his uncle Changqian counts against him."

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「苟或有才，此何所累！」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said, "If there is talent, what burden is this!"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "If the man has talent, what does that matter!"

sentences.zh: 遂拜天官員外郎。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Assistant Director of the Bureau of Celestial Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Xi was thereupon appointed Assistant Director of the Bureau of Celestial Offices.

sentences.zh: 由是諸緣坐者始得進用。

translations.literal: From this, all who had been implicated through association were first able to be promoted and employed.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, those implicated by association were at last allowed to advance and take office.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丁亥，以天官侍郎韋承慶爲鳳閣侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on dinghai, Tian Guan Vice Minister Wei Chengqing was made Fengge Vice Minister and Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on dinghai, Wei Chengqing, Vice Minister of the Bureau of Celestial Offices, was made Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，成均祭酒、同鳳閣鸞臺三品李嶠罷爲地官尚書。

translations.literal: On guimao, Li Jiao, Libationer of the Imperial Academy and Associate Third-Rank Courtier of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, was removed and made Earth Official Minister.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Li Jiao, Libationer of the Imperial Academy and Associate Third-Rank Courtier of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, was dismissed as chancellor and made Minister of the Bureau of Earthly Offices.

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲寅，敕大足已來新置官並停。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jiayin, an edict ordered that all newly established offices since the Dazu era be abolished together.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiayin, an edict abolished all offices created since the Dazu era.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，鳳閣侍郎、同平章事韋嗣立罷爲成均祭酒，檢校魏州刺史如故；

translations.literal: On bingchen, Fengge Vice Minister and Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State Wei Silai was removed and made Libationer of the Imperial Academy, with acting Prefect of Wei Prefecture as before;
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Wei Silai, Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State, was dismissed from the chancellorship and made Libationer of the Imperial Academy, while retaining his acting appointment as Prefect of Wei Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 以兄承慶入相故也。

translations.literal: this was because his elder brother Chengqing had entered the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: this was because his elder brother Chengqing had been made chancellor.

sentences.zh: 太后寢疾，居長生院，宰相不得見者累月，惟張易之、昌宗侍側。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager lay ill and resided in the Everlasting Life Hall; the chancellors could not see her for many months, and only Zhang Yizhi and Changzong attended at her side.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager fell seriously ill and withdrew to the Hall of Everlasting Life; for months the chancellors could not see her, and only Zhang Yizhi and Zhang Changzong waited at her bedside.

sentences.zh: 疾少間，崔玄暐奏言：「皇太子、相王，仁明孝友，足侍湯藥。

translations.literal: When her illness eased a little, Cui Xuanwei memorialized, saying, "The Crown Prince and the Prince of Xiang are benevolent, wise, filial, and fraternal—fit to attend to medicine and broth.
translations.idiomatic: When she improved slightly, Cui Xuanwei memorialized, "The Crown Prince and the Prince of Xiang are benevolent, wise, filial, and brotherly—fully capable of tending your medicine.

sentences.zh: 宮禁事重，伏願不令異姓出入。」

translations.literal: Affairs of the inner palace are weighty; I humbly wish that persons of other surnames not be allowed to come and go."
translations.idiomatic: Palace security is a grave matter; I beg that you not permit outsiders of other surnames to enter and leave at will."

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「德卿厚意。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said, "Your virtuous kindness is deep."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "Your thoughtful concern does you credit."

sentences.zh: 易之、昌宗見太后疾篤，恐禍及己，引用黨援，陰爲之備。

translations.literal: Yizhi and Changzong, seeing the Empress Dowager's illness grave, feared calamity would reach them, recruited partisan allies, and secretly made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the Empress Dowager gravely ill, Yizhi and Changzong feared disaster for themselves, recruited allies, and quietly made ready.

sentences.zh: 屢有人爲飛書及榜其事於通衢，云「易之兄弟謀反」，太后皆不問。

translations.literal: Repeatedly someone wrote anonymous letters and posted the matter on public thoroughfares, saying "The brothers Yizhi are plotting rebellion," but the Empress Dowager in every case made no inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Anonymous letters circulated again and again, and placards appeared in the streets accusing the Zhang brothers of plotting rebellion, but the Empress Dowager ignored every report.

sentences.zh: 辛未，許州人楊元嗣，告「昌宗嘗召術士李弘泰占相，弘泰言昌宗有天子相，勸於定州造佛寺，則天下歸心。」

translations.literal: On xinwei, Yang Yuanci of Xu Prefecture reported, "Changzong once summoned the practitioner Li Hongtai to read his physiognomy. Hongtai said Changzong had the countenance of a Son of Heaven and urged him to build a Buddhist temple at Ding Prefecture, then all under Heaven would turn their hearts to him."
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Yang Yuanci of Xu Prefecture reported that Zhang Changzong had summoned the diviner Li Hongtai to read his physiognomy; Hongtai declared that Changzong bore the countenance of a Son of Heaven and urged him to build a Buddhist temple at Ding Prefecture so that the realm would turn to him."

sentences.zh: 太后命韋承麇慶及司刑卿崔神慶、御史中丞宋璟鞫之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager ordered Wei Chengluqing along with Minister of Punishments Cui Shenqing and Censor-in-Chief Song Jing to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager ordered Wei Chengqing, Minister of Punishments Cui Shenqing, and Censor-in-Chief Song Jing to investigate.

sentences.zh: 神慶，神基之弟也。

translations.literal: Shenqing was the younger brother of Shenji.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqing was the younger brother of Shenji.

sentences.zh: 承慶、神慶奏言：「昌宗款稱『弘泰之語，尋已奏聞」，准法首原；

translations.literal: Chengqing and Shenqing memorialized, saying, "Changzong honestly stated, 'Hongtai's words were soon reported to Your Majesty,' and by law the first offender is pardoned;
translations.idiomatic: Chengqing and Shenqing reported, "Changzong truthfully stated that he had already reported Hongtai's words to Your Majesty; by law the first confession warrants pardon;

sentences.zh: 弘泰妖言，請收行法。」

translations.literal: Hongtai spoke sorcerous words—please arrest him and apply the law."
translations.idiomatic: Hongtai spoke sedition—he should be arrested and punished according to law."

sentences.zh: 璟與大理丞封全禎奏：「昌宗龐榮如是，復召術士占相，志欲何求！

translations.literal: Jing together with Senior Assistant of the Court of Judicial Review Feng Quanzhen memorialized, "Changzong's favor and glory are already so great, yet he again summoned a practitioner to read his physiognomy—what does he seek!
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing and Senior Assistant of the Court of Judicial Review Feng Quanzhen submitted, "Changzong already enjoys immense favor, yet he again summoned a diviner to read his fate—what is he after!

sentences.zh: 弘泰稱筮得純《乾》，天子之卦。

translations.literal: Hongtai said by divination he obtained the pure Hexagram Qian—the hexagram of the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Hongtai claimed that divination had yielded the pure Hexagram Qian—the hexagram of the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 昌宗倘以弘泰爲妖妄，何不即執送有司！

translations.literal: If Changzong regarded Hongtai as sorcerous and deluded, why did he not immediately seize him and deliver him to the authorities!
translations.idiomatic: If Changzong thought Hongtai a fraud, why did he not seize him at once and hand him over to the authorities!

sentences.zh: 雖雲奏聞，終是包藏禍心，法當處斬破家。

translations.literal: Although he says he reported it, in the end he harbors a treacherous heart; by law he should be executed and his household destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Though he claims to have reported the matter, he still harbored treasonous intent; by law he should be executed and his family ruined.

sentences.zh: 請收付獄，窮理其罪！」

translations.literal: Please take him into custody and thoroughly investigate his crime!"
translations.idiomatic: We ask that he be taken into custody and his crime fully investigated!"

sentences.zh: 太后久之不應，璟又曰：「儻不即收系，恐其搖動眾心。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager for a long time did not reply. Jing again said, "If he is not immediately arrested and bound, I fear he may shake the hearts of the multitude."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager long remained silent. Song Jing added, "If he is not arrested immediately, I fear he will unsettle the hearts of the people."

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「卿且停推，俟更檢詳文狀。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said, "You for now halt the investigation and wait until the documents are examined again in detail."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "Stop the investigation for now and wait until the documents are reviewed again."

sentences.zh: 璟退，左拾遺江都李邕進曰：「向觀宋璟所奏，志安社稷，非爲身謀，願陛下可其奏。」

translations.literal: Jing withdrew. Reminder of the Left Li Yong of Jiangdu stepped forward and said, "Just now, observing Song Jing's memorial, his aim is to secure the altars of soil and grain and is not for his own advancement. I wish Your Majesty would approve his memorial."
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing withdrew. Reminder of the Left Li Yong of Jiangdu stepped forward and said, "Song Jing's memorial seeks only the safety of the realm, not personal gain. I urge Your Majesty to approve it."

sentences.zh: 太后不聽。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager would not heed.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager refused.

sentences.zh: 尋敕璟揚州推按，又敕璟按幽州都督屈突仲翔贓污，又敕璟副李嶠安撫隴、蜀；

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered Jing to investigate and examine matters at Yang Prefecture; again an edict ordered Jing to investigate the embezzlement of Military Commissioner of You Prefecture Qu Tu Zhongxiang; again an edict ordered Jing to serve as deputy to Li Jiao in pacifying Long and Shu;
translations.idiomatic: Soon edicts dispatched Song Jing to investigate at Yang Prefecture, to examine the corruption of Qu Tu Zhongxiang, Military Commissioner of You Prefecture, and to serve as deputy to Li Jiao in pacifying Long and Shu;

sentences.zh: 璟皆不肯行，奏曰：「故事，州縣官有罪，品高則侍御史、卑則監察御史按之，中丞非軍國大事，不當出使。

translations.literal: Jing in every case refused to go and memorialized, saying, "By precedent, when an official of prefecture or county has committed an offense, if his rank is high a Palace Censor investigates, if low an Investigation Censor investigates; the Censor-in-Chief, unless there is a great military or state affair, ought not go on mission.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing refused every assignment and memorialized, "By precedent, crimes by prefectural and county officials are investigated by a Palace Censor if the offender's rank is high, and by an Investigation Censor if it is low; the Censor-in-Chief should not go on mission unless the matter is a grave military or state affair.

sentences.zh: 今隴、蜀無變，不識陛下遣臣出外何也？

translations.literal: Now Long and Shu have no disturbance—Your Majesty's sending your subject abroad, what is the reason?
translations.idiomatic: Long and Shu are untroubled now—why is Your Majesty sending me away?

sentences.zh: 臣皆不敢奉制。」

translations.literal: Your subject dares not in any case accept the command."
translations.idiomatic: I dare not obey any of these orders."

sentences.zh: 司刑少卿桓彥范上疏，以爲：「昌宗無功荷寵，而包藏禍心，自招其咎，此乃皇天降怒；

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Punishments Huan Yanfan submitted a memorial, holding that, "Changzong without merit bears favor, yet harbors a treacherous heart and brings calamity upon himself—this is Heaven above lowering its wrath;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Punishments Huan Yanfan submitted a memorial arguing that "Changzong enjoys imperial favor without merit, yet harbors treasonous intent and has brought disaster upon himself—this is Heaven showing its anger;

sentences.zh: 陛下不忍加誅，則違天不祥。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty cannot bear to add execution, then you oppose Heaven—this is inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty shrinks from executing him, you defy Heaven—an ill omen.

sentences.zh: 且昌宗既雲奏訖，則不當更與弘泰往還，使之求福禳災，是則初無悔心；

translations.literal: Moreover, since Changzong has already said the report was finished, he ought not again interact with Hongtai and have him seek blessings and avert calamity—this shows from the first he had no heart of repentance;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if Changzong truly had already reported the matter, he should not still be dealing with Hongtai, having him pray for blessing and avert disaster—this proves he never repented;

sentences.zh: 所以奏者，擬事發則雲先已奏陳，不發則俟時爲逆。

translations.literal: the reason for the report was that, if the affair broke out he could say he had already reported it beforehand, and if it did not break out he could wait for the time and rebel.
translations.idiomatic: his report was a hedge—if the plot surfaced he could claim prior disclosure, and if it did not he could wait for his moment to rebel.

sentences.zh: 此乃奸臣詭計，若雲可捨，誰爲可刑！

translations.literal: This is the cunning scheme of a treacherous minister; if one says this may be set aside, who is there who may be punished!
translations.idiomatic: This is a traitor's trick; if such a man may go unpunished, who could ever be punished!

sentences.zh: 況事已再發，陛下皆釋不問，使昌宗益自負得計，天下亦以爲天命不死，此乃陛下養成其亂也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the affair has erupted twice and Your Majesty in every case released and made no inquiry, causing Changzong to grow even more self-assured that his scheme succeeds, and all under Heaven also to think that by Heaven's mandate he cannot die—this is Your Majesty nurturing his rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The affair has surfaced twice, yet Your Majesty has released him each time, convincing Changzong that his scheme works and leading the realm to believe he is fated to survive—Your Majesty is nurturing rebellion.

sentences.zh: 苟逆臣不誅，社稷亡矣。

translations.literal: If the rebellious minister is not executed, the altars of soil and grain will perish.
translations.idiomatic: If the traitor is not punished, the state will perish.

sentences.zh: 請付鸞臺鳳閣三司，考竟其罪！」

translations.literal: Please hand the case to the Three Offices of the Crane Terrace and Phoenix Pavilion and thoroughly investigate his crime to the end!"
translations.idiomatic: We ask that the Three Offices of the Crane Terrace and Phoenix Pavilion be charged to investigate his crime to the full!"

sentences.zh: 疏奏，不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; no response was given.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 崔玄暐亦屢以爲言，太后令法司議其罪。

translations.literal: Cui Xuanwei also repeatedly spoke thus; the Empress Dowager ordered the legal offices to deliberate on his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuanwei also spoke repeatedly on the matter, and the Empress Dowager ordered the legal offices to determine Changzong's crime.

sentences.zh: 玄□弟司刑少卿忭，處以大辟。

translations.literal: Cui Xuanwei's younger brother, Vice Minister of Punishments Bi, adjudged the capital penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuanwei's younger brother, Vice Minister of Punishments Bi, ruled for execution.

sentences.zh: 宋璟復奏收昌宗下獄。

translations.literal: Song Jing again memorialized to arrest Changzong and send him down to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing again memorialized demanding Changzong be arrested and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「昌宗已自奏聞。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said, "Changzong has already reported himself."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "Changzong already reported the matter himself."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「昌宗爲飛書所逼，窮而自陳，勢非得已。

translations.literal: He replied, "Changzong was driven by anonymous letters, forced to the limit and confessing himself—he had no choice under the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing replied, "Anonymous letters backed him into a corner; he confessed only when he had no choice.

sentences.zh: 且謀反大逆，無容首免。

translations.literal: Moreover, plotting rebellion is great treason; there is no allowing pardon for the first offense.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, treason admits no pardon even for a first confession.

sentences.zh: 若昌宗不伏大刑，安用國法！」

translations.literal: If Changzong does not submit to the great punishment, what use is the law of the state!"
translations.idiomatic: If Changzong does not face the supreme penalty, what use is the law!"

sentences.zh: 太后溫言解之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager with gentle words tried to dissuade him.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager tried to placate him with gentle words.

sentences.zh: 璟聲色逾厲曰：「昌宗分外承恩，臣知言出禍從，然義激於心，雖死不恨！」

translations.literal: Jing, his voice and expression growing ever sterner, said, "Changzong bears favor beyond measure. Your subject knows that words bring calamity in their wake, yet duty stirs the heart—even death brings no regret!"
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing's voice and bearing grew fiercer: "Changzong enjoys favor beyond reason. I know my words invite disaster, but my conscience leaves me no choice—even death would be without regret!"

sentences.zh: 太后不悅，楊再思恐其忤旨，遽宣敕令出，璟曰：「聖主在此，不煩宰相擅宣敕命！」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was displeased. Yang Zaisi, fearing he would defy the imperial will, hastily proclaimed an edict ordering him out. Jing said, "The sage sovereign is present—there is no need for the chancellor on his own authority to proclaim an edict!"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager was displeased. Fearing a breach with the throne, Yang Zaisi hastily proclaimed an edict ordering Song Jing out. Song Jing said, "The sovereign is here—there is no need for a chancellor to proclaim edicts on his own authority!"

sentences.zh: 太后乃可其奏，遣昌宗詣台，璟庭立而按之；

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager then approved his memorial and sent Changzong to the censorate. Jing stood in the court and investigated him;
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager then approved his request and sent Changzong to the censorate, where Song Jing questioned him in open court;

sentences.zh: 事未畢，太后遣中使召昌守特敕赦之。

translations.literal: before the affair was finished, the Empress Dowager sent a palace messenger to summon Chang, keeping the special edict to pardon him.
translations.idiomatic: before the inquiry was finished, the Empress Dowager sent a palace messenger to summon Changzong and pardon him by special edict.

sentences.zh: 璟歎曰：「不先擊小子腦裂，負此恨矣！」

translations.literal: Jing sighed and said, "Not to have smashed that wretch's skull first—I bear this regret!"
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing sighed, "I did not shatter that scoundrel's skull first—this will haunt me!"

sentences.zh: 太后乃使昌宗詣璟謝，璟拒不見。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager then had Changzong go to Jing to apologize; Jing refused to see him.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager then sent Changzong to apologize to Song Jing, but he refused to receive him.

sentences.zh: 左台中丞桓彥范、右台中丞東光袁恕己共薦詹事司直陽嶠爲御史。

translations.literal: Left Censorate Chief Huan Yanfan and Right Censorate Chief Yuan Shuji of Dongguang jointly recommended Chief Clerk of the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent Yang Jiao as censor.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yanfan, Chief of the Left Censorate, and Yuan Shuji of Dongguang, Chief of the Right Censorate, jointly recommended Yang Jiao, Chief Clerk of the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent, for a censorial post.

sentences.zh: 楊再思曰：「嶠不樂搏擊之任如何？」

translations.literal: Yang Zaisi said, "What if Jiao does not enjoy the duty of investigating and impeaching?"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zaisi said, "What if Yang Jiao does not want the investigative role?"

sentences.zh: 彥范曰：「爲官擇人，豈必待其所欲！

translations.literal: Yanfan said, "In appointing men to office, must one wait for what they desire!
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yanfan replied, "When filling offices, must we wait for what candidates want?

sentences.zh: 所不欲者，尤須與之，所以長難進之風，抑躁求之路。」

translations.literal: Those who do not desire it are all the more to be given it—thereby to encourage the wind of difficulty in advancing and restrain the path of rash seeking."
translations.idiomatic: Those who do not seek the post are exactly the ones who should receive it—to nurture a culture in which advancement is difficult and curb the rush for preferment."

sentences.zh: 乃擢爲右台侍御史。

translations.literal: He was then promoted to Attending Censor of the Right Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jiao was thereupon promoted to Attending Censor of the Right Censorate.

sentences.zh: 嶠，休之之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Jiao was the great-great-grandson of Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jiao was the great-great-grandson of Yang Xiuzhi.

sentences.zh: 先是李嶠、崔玄暐奏：「往屬革命之時，人多逆節，遂致刻薄之吏，恣行酷法。

translations.literal: Earlier Li Jiao and Cui Xuanwei memorialized, saying, "In the past, during the Revolution, many people violated propriety, and so harsh officials were let loose to wield cruel laws at will.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Jiao and Cui Xuanwei memorialized that "during the Revolution many people were accused of disloyalty, allowing harsh officials to wield cruel punishments at will.

sentences.zh: 其周興等所劾破家者，並請雪免。」

translations.literal: Those whose households were destroyed through impeachment by Zhou Xing and others—all are requested to be cleared and pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that all whose families were ruined through prosecutions by Zhou Xing and others be cleared and restored."

sentences.zh: 司刑少卿桓彥范又奏陳之，表疏前-{後}-十上，太后乃從之。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Punishments Huan Yanfan again memorialized and set forth the matter; memorials before and after were submitted ten times, and the Empress Dowager then assented.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yanfan, Vice Minister of Punishments, raised the matter again in memorial after memorial—ten submissions in all—before the Empress Dowager finally agreed.

sentences.zh: 中宗大和大聖大昭孝皇帝上

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong, Grand and Harmonious Great Sage Great Manifest Filial—Part One
