translations.idiomatic: Reign of Emperor Zhongzong, the Grand and Harmonious Great Sage Great Manifest Filial Emperor—Part One

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬午朔，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the renwu new moon, there was an amnesty for all under Heaven and the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the renwu new moon, the court proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 自文明以來得罪者，非揚、豫、博三州及諸反逆魁首，鹹赦除之。

translations.literal: Those who had offended since the Wenzming era, except those of Yang, Yu, and Bo Prefectures and the chief leaders of various rebellions, were all universally amnestied and cleared.
translations.idiomatic: All offenders since the Wenzming era, except residents of Yang, Yu, and Bo Prefectures and the ringleaders of rebellion, were fully pardoned.

sentences.zh: 太后疾甚，麟台監張易之、春官侍郎張昌宗居中用事，張柬之、崔玄暐與中台右丞敬暉、司刑少卿桓彥范、相王府司馬袁恕己謀誅之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager's illness was very grave. Palace Library Director Zhang Yizhi and Spring Official Vice Minister Zhang Changzong held power at the center of the court. Zhang Jianzhi, Cui Xuanwei, Right Assistant of the Central Secretariat Jing Hui, Vice Minister of Punishments Huan Yanfan, and Secretariat Major of the Prince of Xiang's household Yuan Shuji plotted to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager was gravely ill. Zhang Yizhi, Director of the Palace Library, and Zhang Changzong, Vice Minister of Spring Offices, wielded power at court. Zhang Jianzhi, Cui Xuanwei, Jing Hui, Right Assistant of the Central Secretariat, Huan Yanfan, Vice Minister of Punishments, and Yuan Shuji, Secretariat Major of the Prince of Xiang's household, plotted to kill them.

sentences.zh: 柬之謂右羽林衞大將軍李多祚曰：「將軍今日富貴，誰所致也？」

translations.literal: Jianzhi said to Right General of the Feathered Forest Guard Li Duozuo, "General, the wealth and honor you enjoy today—by whom were they brought about?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jianzhi said to Li Duozuo, Grand General of the Right Feathered Forest Guard, "General, who made you rich and powerful today?"

sentences.zh: 多祚泣曰：「大帝也。」

translations.literal: Duozuo wept and said, "The Great Emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Duozuo wept and said, "The late Emperor."

sentences.zh: 柬之曰：「今大帝之子爲二豎所危，將軍不思報大帝之德乎？」

translations.literal: Jianzhi said, "Now the Great Emperor's son is endangered by two lackeys—does the General not think to repay the Great Emperor's kindness?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jianzhi said, "The late Emperor's son is now endangered by two worthless favorites—will you not repay the late Emperor's kindness?"

sentences.zh: 多祚曰：「苟利國家，惟相公處分，不敢顧身及妻子！」

translations.literal: Duozuo said, "If it benefits the state, let the Chancellor dispose as he will—I dare not spare body, wife, or children!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Duozuo said, "If it serves the realm, command me as you will—I will not spare myself, my wife, or my children!"

sentences.zh: 因指天地以自誓。

translations.literal: He then pointed to Heaven and Earth to swear himself.
translations.idiomatic: He swore by Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 遂與定謀。

translations.literal: They then finalized the plot together.
translations.idiomatic: They then finalized their plot.

sentences.zh: 初，柬之與荊府長史閺鄕楊元琰相代，同泛江，至中流，語及太后革命事，元琰慨然有匡復之志。

translations.literal: Earlier Jianzhi and Chief Secretary of Jing Prefecture Yang Yuanyan of Minxiang had succeeded each other in office. They floated on the river together, and reaching midstream spoke of the Empress Dowager's Revolution; Yuanyan stirred with resolve to restore the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhang Jianzhi and Yang Yuanyan of Minxiang, Chief Secretary of Jing Prefecture, had succeeded each other in office. Once, boating together, they reached midriver and spoke of the Empress Dowager's seizure of power; Yuanyan was moved by a resolve to restore the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 及柬之爲相，引元琰爲右羽林將軍，謂曰：「君頗記江中之言乎？

translations.literal: When Jianzhi became chancellor, he brought Yuanyan in as General of the Right Feathered Forest Guard and said to him, "Do you quite remember what was said on the river?
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jianzhi became chancellor, he appointed Yuanyan General of the Right Feathered Forest Guard and said, "Do you remember what we said on the river?

sentences.zh: 今日非輕授也。」

translations.literal: Today's appointment is not given lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Today's appointment is no casual gift."

sentences.zh: 柬之又用彥范、暉及右散騎侍郎李湛皆爲左、右羽林將軍，委以禁兵。

translations.literal: Jianzhi also employed Yanfan, Hui, and Right Senior Gentleman Attendant Li Zhan, all as Left and Right Generals of the Feathered Forest Guard, entrusting them with the forbidden troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jianzhi also appointed Yanfan, Hui, and Li Zhan, Right Senior Gentleman Attendant, as generals of the Left and Right Feathered Forest Guard, entrusting them with the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 易之等疑懼，乃更以其黨武攸宜爲右羽林大將軍，易之等乃安。

translations.literal: Yizhi and the others were suspicious and afraid; they then additionally made their partisan Wu Youyi Grand General of the Right Feathered Forest Guard, and only then did Yizhi and the others feel secure.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi and his allies grew fearful and installed their follower Wu Youyi as Grand General of the Right Feathered Forest Guard; only then did they feel secure.

sentences.zh: 俄而姚元之自靈武至都，柬之、彥范相謂曰：「事濟矣！」

translations.literal: Before long Yao Yuanchong arrived at the capital from Lingwu. Jianzhi and Yanfan said to each other, "The affair will succeed!"
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yao Yuanchong returned to the capital from Lingwu. Zhang Jianzhi and Huan Yanfan said to each other, "It will succeed!"

sentences.zh: 遂以其謀告之。

translations.literal: They then told him their plot.
translations.idiomatic: They then revealed their plan to him.

sentences.zh: 彥范以事白其母，母曰：「忠孝不兩全，先國-{後}-家可也。」

translations.literal: Yanfan informed his mother of the affair. His mother said, "Loyalty and filial piety cannot both be fulfilled in full—put the state first and the family after; that will do."
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yanfan told his mother, who said, "Loyalty and filial piety cannot both be fulfilled—serve the state before the family."

sentences.zh: 時太子於北門起居，彥范、暉謁見，密陳其策，太子許之。

translations.literal: At the time the Crown Prince was lodging at the North Gate. Yanfan and Hui paid their respects and privately set forth the strategy; the Crown Prince assented.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince was then staying at the North Gate. Yanfan and Hui visited him, privately laid out the plan, and the Crown Prince agreed.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，柬之、玄□、彥范與左威衞將軍薛思行等，帥左右羽林兵五百餘人至玄武門，遣多祚、湛及內直郎、駙馬都尉安陽王同皎詣東宮迎太子。

translations.literal: On guimao, Jianzhi, Cui Xuanwei, Yanfan, and General of the Left Might Guard Xue Sixing and others led more than five hundred Left and Right Feathered Forest troops to the Xuanwu Gate, dispatching Duozuo, Zhan, and Inner Gentleman Attendant and Commandant of Horse and Imperial Son-in-Law the Prince of Anyang Tong Jiao to the Eastern Palace to welcome the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Zhang Jianzhi, Cui Xuanwei, Huan Yanfan, Xue Sixing, General of the Left Might Guard, and others led more than five hundred Feathered Forest guards to the Xuanwu Gate and sent Duozuo, Li Zhan, and Tong Jiao, the Prince of Anyang, Inner Gentleman Attendant and Commandant of Horse, to the Eastern Palace to escort the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 太子疑，不出，同皎曰：「先帝以神器付殿下，橫遭幽廢，人神同憤，二十三年矣！

translations.literal: The Crown Prince hesitated and would not come out. Tong Jiao said, "The Former Emperor entrusted the sacred vessel to Your Highness; you were wrongly forced into seclusion and dismissal—Heaven and men alike raged together—twenty-three years now!
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince hesitated and refused to come out. Tong Jiao said, "The former Emperor entrusted the throne to Your Highness; you were wrongly deposed—Heaven and men alike have burned with outrage these twenty-three years!

sentences.zh: 今天誘其衷，北門、南牙，同心協力，以今日誅凶豎，復李氏社稷，願殿下暫至玄武門，以副眾望。」

translations.literal: Today Heaven reveals its inner intent; the North Gate and the Southern Office, of one heart and joining force, on this day will execute the wicked lackeys and restore the altars of the Li clan. I wish Your Highness would for the moment come to the Xuanwu Gate to answer the multitude's hope."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has now opened the way; the North Gate and the Southern Office stand united to kill these villains today and restore the Li dynasty. I beg Your Highness to come at once to the Xuanwu Gate and fulfill the people's hopes."

sentences.zh: 太子曰：「凶豎誠當夷滅，然上體不安，得無驚怛！

translations.literal: The Crown Prince said, "The wicked lackeys truly ought to be exterminated root and branch, but the Sovereign's health is frail—would this not startle and alarm her!
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince said, "Those villains truly deserve extermination, but the Empress Dowager's health is fragile—would we not terrify her?

sentences.zh: 諸公更爲-{後}-圖。」

translations.literal: Let the lords devise another plan for afterward."
translations.idiomatic: Let the lords plan another course for later."

sentences.zh: 李湛曰：「諸將相不顧家族以徇社稷，殿下奈何欲納之鼎鑊乎！

translations.literal: Li Zhan said, "The generals and chief ministers have risked their families to serve the altars of state—how can Your Highness wish to hand them over to the cauldron and furnace!
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhan said, "The generals and chief ministers have staked their families on the realm—how can Your Highness mean to deliver them to execution!

sentences.zh: 請殿下自出止之。」

translations.literal: I beg Your Highness to go out yourself and stop them."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Highness to go out yourself and restrain them."

sentences.zh: 太子乃出。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince then came out.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince then emerged.

sentences.zh: 同皎扶抱太子上馬，從至玄武門，斬關而入。

translations.literal: Tong Jiao supported and embraced the Crown Prince to mount his horse, followed him to the Xuanwu Gate, cut through the barrier, and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Jiao helped the Crown Prince into the saddle, accompanied him to the Xuanwu Gate, forced the pass, and entered.

sentences.zh: 太后在迎仙宮，柬之等斬易之、昌宗於廡下，進至太后所寢長生殿，環繞侍衞。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was at the Yingxian Palace. Jianzhi and the others executed Yizhi and Changzong beneath the corridor eaves, advanced to the Changsheng Hall where the Empress Dowager slept, and surrounded her in attendance and guard.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager was at the Yingxian Palace. Zhang Jianzhi and his allies cut down Yizhi and Changzong under the corridor eaves, then pressed on to the Changsheng Hall, her sleeping quarters, and formed a ring of guards around her.

sentences.zh: 太后驚起，問曰：「亂者誰邪？」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager started up in alarm and asked, "Who are the rioters?"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager started up in fright and asked, "Who is making this disturbance?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「張易之、昌宗謀反，臣等奉太子令誅之，恐有漏洩，故不敢以聞。

translations.literal: They replied, "Zhang Yizhi and Changzong plotted rebellion; we, your ministers, received the Crown Prince's order to execute them; fearing a leak, we dared not report it beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "Zhang Yizhi and Changzong plotted rebellion. We acted on the Crown Prince's orders to kill them and dared not report it beforehand for fear word would leak out.

sentences.zh: 稱兵宮禁，罪當萬死！」

translations.literal: To raise troops within the palace precincts—the crime merits ten thousand deaths!"
translations.idiomatic: Raising arms within the palace is a crime deserving death a thousand times over!"

sentences.zh: 太后見太子曰：「乃汝邪？

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager saw the Crown Prince and said, "So it is you?
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager looked at the Crown Prince and said, "So it is you?

sentences.zh: 小子既誅，可還東宮！」

translations.literal: The wicked boys are already executed—you may return to the Eastern Palace!"
translations.idiomatic: Now that those villains are dead, you may go back to the Eastern Palace!"

sentences.zh: 彥范進曰：「太子安得更歸！

translations.literal: Yanfan stepped forward and said, "How can the Crown Prince return again!
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yanfan stepped forward and said, "The Crown Prince cannot go back!

sentences.zh: 昔天皇以愛子托陛下，今年齒已長，久居東宮，天意人心，久思李氏。

translations.literal: Formerly the Heavenly Sovereign entrusted his beloved son to Your Majesty; now his years are already many and he has long dwelt in the Eastern Palace—Heaven's intent and the people's hearts have long yearned for the House of Li.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the Heavenly Sovereign entrusted his beloved son to Your Majesty; he is mature in years and has long waited in the Eastern Palace. Heaven's intent and the people's hearts have long turned toward the House of Li.

sentences.zh: 群臣不忘太宗、天皇之德，故奉太子誅賊臣。

translations.literal: Your ministers have not forgotten the virtue of Emperor Taizong and the Heavenly Sovereign; therefore we have followed the Crown Prince in executing the traitorous ministers.
translations.idiomatic: We have not forgotten the grace of Emperor Taizong and the Heavenly Sovereign, and so we followed the Crown Prince in killing these traitors.

sentences.zh: 願陛下傳位太子，以順天人之望！」

translations.literal: We wish Your Majesty to transmit the throne to the Crown Prince, to accord with Heaven and men's hopes!"
translations.idiomatic: We beg Your Majesty to abdicate in favor of the Crown Prince and fulfill the hopes of Heaven and the people!"

sentences.zh: 李湛，義府之子也。

translations.literal: Li Zhan was the son of Yifu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhan was the son of Li Yifu.

sentences.zh: 太后見之，謂曰：「汝亦爲誅易之將軍邪？

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager saw him, she said to him, "Are you also a general in the execution of Yizhi?
translations.idiomatic: When she saw him, she said, "So you too are among the generals who killed Yizhi?

sentences.zh: 我於汝父子不薄，乃有今日！」

translations.literal: I have not treated you and your father shabbily—yet this is what comes of it today!"
translations.idiomatic: I have been generous to you and your father—yet this is how you repay me!"

sentences.zh: 湛慚不能對。

translations.literal: Zhan was ashamed and could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhan flushed with shame and had no answer.

sentences.zh: 又謂崔玄暐曰：「他人皆因人以進，惟卿朕所自擢，亦在此邪？」

translations.literal: She also said to Cui Xuanwei, "Others all advanced through someone's recommendation—only you I myself promoted. Are you here as well?"
translations.idiomatic: She then turned to Cui Xuanwei and said, "Others all rose through patrons—but you I promoted myself. You are here too?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「此乃所以報陛下之大德。」

translations.literal: He replied, "This is precisely how I repay Your Majesty's great kindness."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "This is my repayment for Your Majesty's great kindness."

sentences.zh: 於是收張昌期、同休、昌儀等，皆斬之，與易之、昌宗梟首天津南。

translations.literal: Thereupon Changqi, Tongxiu, Changyi, and the others were arrested and all beheaded; together with Yizhi and Changzong their heads were displayed on poles south of the Tianjin Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: They then arrested Zhang Changqi, Tongxiu, Changyi, and the rest, beheaded them all, and displayed their heads together with Yizhi's and Changzong's south of the Tianjin Bridge.

sentences.zh: 是日，袁恕己從相王統南牙兵以備非常，收韋承慶、房融及司禮卿崔神慶繫獄，皆易之之黨也。

translations.literal: That day Yuan Shuji, following the Prince of Xiang, commanded the Southern Office troops to guard against the unexpected, and arrested Wei Chengqing, Fang Rong, and Director of Ceremonies Cui Shenqing and imprisoned them—they were all partisans of Yizhi.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Yuan Shuji, with the Prince of Xiang, took command of the Southern Office troops as a precaution, and had Wei Chengqing, Fang Rong, and Cui Shenqing, Director of Ceremonies, seized and imprisoned—all partisans of Yizhi.

sentences.zh: 初，昌儀新作第，甚美，逾於王主。

translations.literal: Earlier Changyi had built a new mansion, very beautiful, surpassing those of royal princesses.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Changyi had built a new residence so splendid it outshone even the palaces of imperial princesses.

sentences.zh: 或夜書其門曰：「一日絲能作幾日絡？」

translations.literal: Someone by night wrote on his gate, saying, "One day's thread—how many days of netting can it make?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone wrote on his gate one night: "One day's worry—how many days of joy can it buy?"

sentences.zh: 滅去，復書之，如是六七。

translations.literal: It was erased and written again, thus six or seven times.
translations.idiomatic: It was scrubbed away and written again, six or seven times over.

sentences.zh: 昌儀取筆注其下曰：「一日亦足。」

translations.literal: Changyi took up a brush and wrote beneath it, "One day is also enough."
translations.idiomatic: Changyi added beneath it in his own hand, "One day is enough."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Only then did it stop.
translations.idiomatic: That put an end to it.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，制太子監國，赦天下。

translations.literal: On jiachen an edict made the Crown Prince regent over the state and amnestied all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen the Crown Prince was ordered to oversee the realm, and an amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 以袁恕己爲鳳閣侍郎、同平章事，分遣十使繼璽書宣慰諸州。

translations.literal: Yuan Shuji was made Phoenix Pavilion Vice Minister and Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State; ten envoys were dispatched in succession with imperial rescripts to proclaim consolation to the various prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shuji was made Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State, and ten envoys were sent out in succession with imperial edicts to reassure the provinces.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，太后傳位於太子。

translations.literal: On yisi the Empress Dowager transmitted the throne to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi the Empress Dowager abdicated in favor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 丙午，中宗即位。

translations.literal: On bingwu Emperor Zhongzong ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu Emperor Zhongzong took the throne.

sentences.zh: 赦天下，惟張易之黨不原；

translations.literal: He amnestied all under Heaven, excepting only Zhang Yizhi's faction from pardon;
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty, except for Zhang Yizhi's faction;

sentences.zh: 其爲周興等所枉者，咸令清雪，子女配沒者皆免之。

translations.literal: Those who had been wronged by Zhou Xing and the others were all ordered cleared of stigma; sons and daughters who had been enslaved through punishment were all released.
translations.idiomatic: Those wrongfully condemned by Zhou Xing and his like were cleared, and children enslaved through criminal punishment were all freed.

sentences.zh: 相王加號安國相王，拜太尉、同鳳閣鸞臺三品，太平公主加號鎮國太平公主。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiang was given the additional title Prince of Xiang Who Pacifies the State, appointed Grand Marshal and Third-Rank Peer of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luantai; the Princess Taiping was given the additional title Princess Taiping Who Stabilizes the State.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xiang received the augmented title Pacifier of the State Prince of Xiang and was appointed Grand Marshal and Third-Rank Peer of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luantai; Princess Taiping received the augmented title Stabilizer of the State Princess Taiping.

sentences.zh: 皇族先配沒者，子孫皆復屬籍，仍量敘官爵。

translations.literal: Among the imperial clan previously enslaved through punishment, descendants were all restored to the registers of lineage, and offices and ranks were granted according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants of imperial clansmen who had been enslaved were restored to the family registers and given offices and ranks as appropriate.

sentences.zh: 丁未，太后徙居上陽宮，李湛留宿衞。

translations.literal: On dingwei the Empress Dowager moved to the Shangyang Palace; Li Zhan remained to keep night watch as guard.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei the Empress Dowager moved to the Shangyang Palace, with Li Zhan left behind to guard her at night.

sentences.zh: 戊申，帝帥百官詣上陽宮，上太后尊號曰則天大聖皇帝。

translations.literal: On wushen the Emperor led the hundred officials to the Shangyang Palace and bestowed on the Empress Dowager the honorific title Empress Zetian the Great Sage Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen the Emperor led the full court to the Shangyang Palace and honored the Empress Dowager with the title Great Sage Emperor Zetian.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以張柬之爲夏官尚書、同鳳閣鸞臺三品，崔玄暐爲內史，袁恕己同鳳閣鸞臺三品，敬暉、桓彥范皆爲納言；

translations.literal: On gengxu Zhang Jianzhi was made Summer Office Director and Third-Rank Peer of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luantai; Cui Xuanwei was made Inner Scribe; Yuan Shuji was made Third-Rank Peer of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luantai; Jing Hui and Huan Yanfan were both made Counselors;
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu Zhang Jianzhi was made Director of the Bureau of Summer Offices and Third-Rank Peer of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luantai; Cui Xuanwei was made Inner Scribe; Yuan Shuji was made Third-Rank Peer of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luantai; Jing Hui and Huan Yanfan were both made Counselors;

sentences.zh: 並賜爵郡公。

translations.literal: All were also granted the nobility rank of Regional Duke.
translations.idiomatic: All were granted the rank of Regional Duke.

sentences.zh: 李多祚賜爵遼陽郡王，王同皎爲右千牛將軍、琅邪郡公，李湛爲右羽林大將軍、趙國公；

translations.literal: Li Duozuo was granted the nobility of Prince of Liaoyang Commandery; the Prince of Anyang Tong Jiao was made Right Thousand-Ox General and Duke of Langya Commandery; Li Zhan was made Right Grand General of the Feathered Forest Guard and Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Duozuo was enfeoffed as Prince of Liaoyang; Tong Jiao, Prince of Anyang, was made Right Thousand-Ox General and Duke of Langya; Li Zhan was made Right Grand General of the Feathered Forest Guard and Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 自餘官賞有差。

translations.literal: The remaining offices and rewards varied in degree.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining awards varied by rank.

sentences.zh: 張柬之等之討張易之也，殿中監田歸道將千騎宿玄武門，敬暉遣使就索千騎，歸道先不預謀，拒而不與。

translations.literal: When Zhang Jianzhi and the others were attacking Zhang Yizhi, Palace Supervisor Tian Guidao was encamped at the Xuanwu Gate with a thousand riders; Jing Hui sent a messenger to demand the thousand riders; Guidao had not been privy to the plot beforehand and refused to give them.
translations.idiomatic: During the coup against Zhang Yizhi, Palace Supervisor Tian Guidao held the Xuanwu Gate with a thousand cavalry. Jing Hui sent to demand the troops, but Guidao, who had not been in on the plot, refused.

sentences.zh: 事寧，暉欲誅之，歸道以理自陳，乃免歸私第；

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, Hui wished to execute him; Guidao stated his case on principle, and so was dismissed to his private residence;
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored, Hui wanted him killed, but Guidao pleaded his case on principle and was merely sent home;

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其忠壯，召拜太僕少卿。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his loyalty and steadfastness, summoned him, and appointed him Vice Director of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor admired his loyalty and courage and summoned him to serve as Vice Director of the Imperial Stud.
